alert.headline: Say what happened, and what to do next.

alert.rtl: The icon leads at the start; actions align to the end.
alert.when_not: For confirmations that can disappear; use a toast.
alert.do_1: Lead with the outcome in the title.
alert.do_2: Offer the next step as an action.
alert.dont_1: Do not use danger tone for neutral news.
alert.dont_2: Do not show several alerts for one problem.

alert_dialog.headline: Pause before the irreversible.
alert_dialog.intro: A focused dialog that asks to confirm or cancel, with the safe choice focused first.

alert_dialog.do_3: Use the danger tone only when the action destroys data.

gallery.when_not: For a single hero picture; use a card or an image.
gallery.do_1: Give each picture its width and height, so a masonry keeps its shape while loading.
gallery.do_2: Use a small thumbnail source for big galleries.
gallery.dont_1: Do not mix the grid and the masonry on one page.
gallery.dont_2: Do not crop faces in the square grid; use the masonry.

alternative.carousel: To show one picture at a time.
alternative.lightbox: To open pictures from a layout of your own.

image_cropper.headline: The right part of the picture.
image_cropper.intro: People drag the picture into the frame and zoom with the slider or the keyboard; you get the kept rectangle in the image's own pixels.
image_cropper.what: A frame that picks the part of an image to keep.
image_cropper.when: Use it for profile photos, logos, covers and product images with a fixed shape.
image_cropper.rtl: Moving is spatial, so the arrow keys move the picture the way they point in every language.
image_cropper.when_not: For free-form edits such as rotation or filters; use an image editor.
image_cropper.do_1: Match the frame to where the picture will show.
image_cropper.do_2: Cut the file on the server from the reported rectangle.
image_cropper.dont_1: Do not crop without showing the result.
image_cropper.dont_2: Do not lock the zoom at one level.

alternative.drop_zone: To pick the file before cropping.

checkbox.headline: A clear yes or no.
checkbox.intro: A checkbox with label and description, indeterminate state and a check that animates in.
checkbox.what: Turns one option on or off.
checkbox.when: Use it for choices confirmed with a submit.
checkbox.rtl: The box leads at the start of its label.
checkbox.when_not: For settings that apply at once; use a switch.
checkbox.do_1: Write the label as the positive choice.
checkbox.do_2: Use the indeterminate state for a partial group.
checkbox.dont_1: Do not use a checkbox for one-of-many choices.
checkbox.dont_2: Do not make the label alone unclickable.

alternative.switch: When the change applies at once.

checkbox_button_group.headline: Pick several, see every choice.
checkbox_button_group.intro: A title and a line of detail on each card let people compare before they tick.
checkbox_button_group.what: A group of cards that each toggle on or off.
checkbox_button_group.when: Use it when a few choices each need a sentence of explanation.
checkbox_button_group.rtl: Cards flow from the start and the check sits at the start edge.

checkbox_group.headline: Choose several, clearly.
checkbox_group.intro: A labelled set of checkboxes with shared validation and a group description.
checkbox_group.when: Use it for several independent options.
checkbox_group.rtl: Options align to the start; boxes lead each label.

chip.headline: Label, filter and tag in a compact pill.
chip.intro: Small pills for tags, filters and statuses with optional icons and a remove action, in soft or solid tones.
chip.what: A compact label for a tag, filter or status.
chip.when: Use it for short labels people scan or remove.
chip.rtl: Start and end icons swap sides; the remove button stays at the end.
chip.do_1: Keep labels to one or two words.
chip.do_2: Use a remove button for removable chips.
chip.dont_1: Do not rely on colour alone for meaning.
chip.dont_2: Do not wrap chips to many lines in tables.

alternative.badge: For a count on another element.

close_button.headline: Closing is one tap, in the same place every time.
close_button.intro: A ready-made close control with its accessible name built in, sized for touch and placed at the end of any panel.
close_button.what: An icon button that dismisses a panel, dialog or message.
close_button.when: Use it in the top end corner of anything that can be dismissed.
close_button.rtl: It sits at the end edge, so it moves to the left in Arabic.

coach_mark.headline: Show new people around, one step at a time.
coach_mark.intro: An onboarding tour that spotlights each element with a callout, skippable and keyboard friendly.
coach_mark.when: Use it for first runs and new features.
coach_mark.rtl: Callouts open toward the inside of the screen in both directions.

code_block.headline: Code that reads as clearly as prose.
code_block.intro: Syntax colours from your theme, line numbers, highlighted lines, diffs and one-press copy make every snippet easy to follow and reuse. Long files show in full behind “Show all”, never in a cramped scroll box.
code_block.what: A styled, copyable block of code or data.
code_block.when: Use it for API examples, webhook payloads and setup steps.
code_block.rtl: Code always runs left to right; only the frame and the copy button follow Arabic.

color_picker.headline: The exact colour, however you think of it.
color_picker.intro: Every route lands on the same value, so the colour people see is the colour they save.
color_picker.what: A control for choosing one colour.
color_picker.when: Use it for brand colours, labels and theme settings.
color_picker.rtl: The hue strip and the hex code stay left to right; swatches flow from the start.

combo_box.headline: Type to find, pick to confirm.
combo_box.intro: A text field with filtered suggestions, async loading and custom values when allowed.
combo_box.when: Use it for long lists people search rather than scroll.
combo_box.rtl: The trigger sits at the end; typed Arabic filters correctly.
combo_box.when_not: For short lists people can scan; use a select.
combo_box.do_1: Match anywhere in the label, not just the start.
combo_box.dont_1: Do not accept free text unless it is allowed.
combo_box.dont_2: Do not open the list before people interact.

alternative.entity_picker: For records with avatars and details.

command_palette.headline: Everything, one keystroke away.
command_palette.intro: Pages and actions sit in one list, so people never hunt through menus again.
command_palette.what: A searchable list of pages and actions in a dialog.
command_palette.when: Use it in dense apps where people know what they want and want it now.
command_palette.rtl: Results and their icons align to the start; shortcut keys keep their own order.

comment_thread.headline: Decide together, right where the work is.
comment_thread.intro: Every voice stays in order beside the work, and the decision is easy to find later.
comment_thread.what: A conversation attached to one item.
comment_thread.when: Use it on orders, documents or changes that need a discussion and a decision.
comment_thread.rtl: Avatars sit at the start, replies indent toward the end, and times read naturally in Arabic.

composed_chart.headline: Two stories on one axis.
composed_chart.intro: One shared scale means the gap between plan and result is visible at once.
composed_chart.what: Columns and lines over one category axis, with an optional second value axis for a measure of a different size.
composed_chart.when: Use it to compare an amount with a goal or a rate over time.
composed_chart.rtl: Time runs from the right in Arabic and the value axis moves to the start side.

context_menu.headline: The right action, right where you clicked.
context_menu.intro: Power users move faster, and nothing is hidden from people who never right-click.
context_menu.what: A menu of actions for the item under the pointer, or under a finger's long press on a phone.
context_menu.when: Use it for secondary actions on rows, cards and files.
context_menu.rtl: Items align to the start and submenus open toward the end.

disclosure.headline: Details when they are wanted.
disclosure.intro: The page stays short, and the delivery terms, advanced settings or fine print are one press away.
disclosure.what: One titled section that opens and closes.
disclosure.when: Use it for one optional block: advanced settings, terms, more about a product.
disclosure.rtl: The chevron sits at the left end in Arabic, and the title reads from the right.
disclosure.when_not: For several sections side by side; use an accordion.
disclosure.do_1: Say in the title what opens.
disclosure.do_2: Start it open when most people need it.
disclosure.dont_1: Do not hide a required field in it.
disclosure.dont_2: Do not nest one inside another.

alternative.accordion: For a list of sections that open and close.
alternative.popover: For a short note over the page, not in its flow.

navigation_menu.headline: Every page, two presses away.
navigation_menu.intro: Visitors see the sections at a glance and open a panel for the pages in each, by mouse, touch or keyboard.
navigation_menu.what: A top bar of links whose entries can open panels of links.
navigation_menu.when: Use it for the main navigation of a website or a wide back office.
navigation_menu.rtl: In Arabic the bar starts on the right, and panels open under their entry toward the left.
navigation_menu.when_not: For a phone app; use the tab bar or a navigation list.
navigation_menu.do_1: Keep the bar to seven entries or fewer.
navigation_menu.do_2: Give each link in a panel a short line.
navigation_menu.dont_1: Do not put actions in it; it is for places.
navigation_menu.dont_2: Do not nest panels inside panels.

alternative.navigation_list: For a side menu of many places.

layout.headline: Spacing that adds up.
layout.intro: Columns, rows and gaps come from one scale, so every screen lines up and mirrors in Arabic with no custom CSS.
layout.what: Four primitives: a column (Stack), a wrapping row (Cluster), equal columns (Grid) and a centred measure (Center).
layout.when: Use them for the space between blocks, wherever a component does not already own it.
layout.rtl: Rows and grids fill from the right in Arabic, and Center is the same both ways.
layout.when_not: For a page with a side column; use the two-column layout.
layout.do_1: Pick a gap from the scale, not a pixel value.
layout.do_2: Give Grid a minimum width so it reflows on a phone.
layout.dont_1: Do not add margins to children to space them.
layout.dont_2: Do not use Grid for a table of data.

alternative.two_column_layout: For a main column with a side column.
alternative.single_column_layout: For a detail page of stacked sections.

contextual_help.headline: Answers right where questions come up.
contextual_help.intro: A small info button that opens a short explanation and a link to learn more.
contextual_help.what: A help button that opens a short explanation.
contextual_help.when: Use it next to terms and settings that need a word of context.
contextual_help.rtl: It follows the label at its end; the popover opens inward.

copy_button.headline: Copy it once, and know it worked.
copy_button.intro: One press copies the value and swaps the icon for a check, with a polite announcement for screen readers.
copy_button.what: A button that copies a value to the clipboard.
copy_button.when: Use it beside codes, links, IDs and keys people paste elsewhere.
copy_button.rtl: Copied values keep their own direction; codes and IDs stay left to right.

country_select.headline: Every country, in the reader's own words.
country_select.intro: Flags and search help people find their country in a second.
country_select.when: Use it in addresses, phone numbers and shipping settings.
country_select.rtl: Names sort by Arabic order in Arabic and the flag leads at the start.

cursor_pagination.headline: Paging that scales to millions.
cursor_pagination.intro: Previous and next over a cursor-based list, fast and stable however large the data grows.
cursor_pagination.what: Previous and next paging over a cursor.
cursor_pagination.when: Use it for large or live lists from cursor APIs.
cursor_pagination.rtl: Previous and next arrows mirror in Arabic.

data_grid.headline: Spreadsheet speed, with guard rails.
data_grid.intro: Mistakes are caught before saving, and every change can be undone. Its typed editors and rules also edit a DataTable's marked cells in place, and its rows are virtualised, so ten thousand stay quick.
data_grid.tags: Ranges · Paste · Validation · Undo · Pin and resize
data_grid.what: An editable grid of typed cells with a save bar.
data_grid.when: Use it for bulk edits of prices, stock or schedules; on a phone it becomes a list with quick edit.
data_grid.rtl: Columns start from the right in Arabic and the fill handle follows; numbers keep their digits' direction.

data_table.headline: Find, sort, arrange and act on records fast.
data_table.intro: Multi-sort, selection with select all across pages (unticked rows stay out), row actions on hover and right-click, rows you drag, expand, open in a side panel or edit in place, pinned and resizable columns, a column editor, density and a totals footer in one accessible grid on the collection engine; with virtual scrolling it draws ten thousand rows and more, header and start pins in place.
data_table.tags: Multi-sort · Column editor · Drag rows · Expand · Inline edit · Side panel · Totals · 10k rows
data_table.what: A table with sorting, selection and row actions.
data_table.when: Use it for lists of records people search, compare and act on.
data_table.rtl: Columns start from the right in Arabic; numbers keep their alignment.
data_table.when_not: For a handful of static rows; use a table.
data_table.do_1: Keep the first column as the record's name.
data_table.dont_1: Do not put more than one primary action per row.

date_field.headline: Type a date, in any calendar, without a fight.
date_field.intro: Segmented day, month and year that accept typing and arrow keys, in the locale's order and digits.
date_field.what: A segmented field for typing a date.
date_field.when: Use it when people know the date and type it faster than picking.
date_field.rtl: Segments follow the locale's order; the field stays isolated in Arabic text.

date_label.headline: Dates that tell you what matters.
date_label.intro: A date as a chip that flags due soon, overdue and expiry, with relative time and the Hijri calendar.
date_label.what: A date shown as a chip with states.
date_label.when: Use it for due dates, expiries and timestamps in lists.
date_label.rtl: Relative phrases read naturally in Arabic; the Hijri date uses its own month names.

date_picker.headline: Pick the right day, first time.
date_picker.intro: A typed date field with a calendar popover, keyboard friendly and correct in every locale.
date_picker.what: A date field with a calendar popover.
date_picker.when: Use it when people need to see the week or month to choose.
date_picker.rtl: The calendar's weeks run from the right; previous and next arrows mirror.
date_picker.when_not: For dates far in the past, such as birth dates; use a date field.
date_picker.do_1: Allow typing as well as picking.
date_picker.do_2: Block unavailable dates with a reason.
date_picker.dont_1: Do not force a single date format.
date_picker.dont_2: Do not hide the year when it matters.

alternative.date_field: When people type a known date.
alternative.date_label: To show a date, not edit it.

date_range_picker.headline: From this day to that, in two taps.
date_range_picker.intro: Ready ranges save taps, and the calendar is there when a custom period is needed.
date_range_picker.what: A field for a range of days.
date_range_picker.when: Use it for reports, bookings and filters by period.
date_range_picker.rtl: The calendar's weeks run from the right; the range reads start to end in Arabic order.

date_time_picker.headline: The day and the hour, set once.
date_time_picker.intro: Keeping both in one field means an appointment never loses half its meaning.
date_time_picker.what: A field for a date and a time of day.
date_time_picker.when: Use it for appointments, deliveries and scheduled sends.
date_time_picker.rtl: The date and time follow Arabic order and the calendar runs from the right.

diff_review.headline: Nothing lands until you approve it.
diff_review.intro: Each change is accepted or rejected on its own, then applied together.
diff_review.what: A list of proposed changes to review.
diff_review.when: Use it for imports, synced data and suggested edits that need a human yes.
diff_review.rtl: Before and after swap sides in Arabic; values keep their own direction.

donut_chart.headline: Show the share and the total at once.
donut_chart.intro: Segments around a ring with the total in the centre and small gaps between parts, readable at any size.
donut_chart.what: A ring chart of parts around their total.
donut_chart.when: Use it for a few parts of one whole, when the total matters too.
donut_chart.rtl: Segments follow the reading direction; the centre total keeps its digits.

drawer.headline: More room, without leaving the page.
drawer.intro: A floating panel with a header, an optional sub-header, a scrolling body and a footer. Open one drawer from another to stack them, or drill into views inside one.
drawer.what: A panel that floats in from the edge, clear of the screen's sides.
drawer.when: Use it for details, filters and forms beside the page.
drawer.rtl: Side drawers open from the end edge, so they slide in from the left in Arabic; the Back chevron points right.
drawer.when_not: For a quick yes or no; use an alert dialog.
drawer.do_1: Use it for details and forms tied to the page.
drawer.do_2: Keep the primary action at the end of the footer, with Cancel before it.
drawer.dont_1: Do not stack more than three drawers; drill into views instead.
drawer.dont_2: Do not put whole workflows in a drawer.

alternative.route_overlay: When the drawer should have its own URL.

drop_zone.headline: Drop it here and you're done.
drop_zone.intro: Drop a file, paste a screenshot, pick one or take a photo; clear limits and a preview of each file mean no upload is a mystery.
drop_zone.what: An area that accepts dropped, pasted, picked or photographed files.
drop_zone.when: Use it wherever people attach invoices, images or spreadsheets.
drop_zone.rtl: The icon and text centre the same in Arabic; file names keep their own direction.

attachment_card.headline: Every file, at a glance.
attachment_card.intro: People see what a file is, how big it is and whether it arrived, and open, download or remove it in place.
attachment_card.what: One attached file with its type, size, upload state and actions.
attachment_card.when: In messages, comments, orders and records that carry files.
attachment_card.rtl: The row mirrors in Arabic; a Latin file name keeps its own order.
attachment_card.when_not: To pick or drop files; use the drop zone.
attachment_card.do_1: Show the size, so people know what they download.
attachment_card.do_2: Say why an upload failed and offer a retry.
attachment_card.dont_1: Don't rename the file in the card.
attachment_card.dont_2: Don't hide the remove button in a menu.

alternative.file_trigger: A button that opens the file picker.

share_button.headline: Share it the way people already do.
share_button.intro: On a phone the system sheet opens with every app people use; on a desktop without one, the link is copied and the button says so.
share_button.what: A button that shares a link, a title and a line of text.
share_button.when: On products, orders, invoices and pages people send to others.
share_button.rtl: The icon sits at the start in Arabic; the link keeps its own direction.
share_button.when_not: To copy a code or a key; use the copy button.
share_button.do_1: Share a link that opens without signing in when you can.
share_button.do_2: Give the share a title people recognise.
share_button.dont_1: Don't put more than one share button on a card.
share_button.dont_2: Don't share links that expire within minutes.

alternative.copy_button: To copy a value without sharing it.
alternative.button: For an action that is not sharing.

emoji_picker.headline: The right feeling in one tap.
emoji_picker.intro: Recently used emoji stay on top, so the favourite is always one tap away.
emoji_picker.when: Use it in messages, reactions and labels.
emoji_picker.rtl: The grid fills from the right in Arabic and the category tabs follow.

empty_state.headline: Turn an empty screen into a first step.
empty_state.intro: A friendly illustration, a clear sentence and the one action that fills the view.
empty_state.what: What a view shows when it has nothing yet.
empty_state.when: Use it for first runs, cleared filters and empty searches.
empty_state.rtl: Text centres in both directions; the action follows the reading order.

entity_picker.headline: Find the right record in a few keys.
entity_picker.intro: Search and pick people, products or any record, with avatars, details and recent picks.
entity_picker.what: A picker for records such as people or products.
entity_picker.when: Use it to assign, link or mention records.
entity_picker.rtl: Avatars lead at the start; Latin names are isolated.

environment_banner.headline: Always know where you are working.
environment_banner.intro: A slim banner that names staging, demo or test, so nobody mistakes it for production.
environment_banner.what: A banner that names the environment.
environment_banner.when: Use it on every non-production environment.
environment_banner.rtl: The label reads from the start; environment names stay as written.

error_page.headline: Even the dead ends point the way home.
error_page.intro: Ready-made 403, 404, 500 and offline pages with a plain explanation and a retry that waits for the network.
error_page.when: Use it for routes that fail as a whole.
error_page.rtl: Text and actions follow the reading direction; codes stay Latin.

error_state.headline: When loading fails, offer a way forward.
error_state.intro: A short reason and a retry inside the view that failed, so the rest of the page keeps working.
error_state.what: What a view shows when loading fails.
error_state.when: Use it for a section or widget that could not load.
error_state.rtl: Content centres; the retry button follows the reading order.

export_dialog.headline: Export exactly what you need.
export_dialog.intro: Choose a format, the columns and the scope, then export, with progress for large files.
export_dialog.what: A dialog that configures and runs an export.
export_dialog.when: Use it on tables and reports that can be exported.
export_dialog.rtl: Column names read in Arabic; file names stay Latin.

fab.headline: The main action, always within reach.
fab.intro: It stays within the thumb's reach, and a speed dial keeps related actions close.
fab.what: A floating button for a screen's main action.
fab.when: Use it on mobile screens with one clear next step, such as new order or add item. While it floats, a bottom toast on a phone rises above it rather than covering it.
fab.rtl: The button floats at the end corner, which is the left in Arabic.

file_trigger.headline: Upload from anywhere, and see it land.
file_trigger.intro: Opens the file, camera or photo picker and lists uploads with progress, retry and remove.
file_trigger.what: A trigger that opens file pickers and lists uploads.
file_trigger.when: Use it for attachments, avatars and imports.
file_trigger.rtl: File names are isolated so extensions stay in place.

filter_bar.headline: Narrow any list in seconds.
filter_bar.intro: A row of filters above a list or table, with clear active chips and a reset, that wraps neatly on small screens.
filter_bar.what: A row of filters above a list or table.
filter_bar.when: Use it when people filter by a few common fields.
filter_bar.rtl: Filters fill from the start; reset sits at the end.

filter_panel.headline: Every facet, with counts, in one panel.
filter_panel.intro: Facets with result counts and saved views, so people narrow large data sets and come back to them later.
filter_panel.what: A panel of filter facets with counts and saved views.
filter_panel.when: Use it beside large lists where people combine many filters.
filter_panel.rtl: The panel opens from the start edge and its counts sit at the end.

flip_card.headline: Two sides of the story in one card.
flip_card.intro: Details, a price or an answer wait on the back until people want them.
flip_card.what: A card with a front and a back.
flip_card.when: Use it for quick reveals: product details, quiz answers or plan comparisons.
flip_card.rtl: The card turns the other way in Arabic so it still flips toward the reader.

form.headline: Forms that guide people to done.
form.intro: Fields, validation and submit in one flow, with errors that say how to fix them and focus that goes to the first one.
form.what: A container that validates and submits fields.
form.when: Use it for any set of fields that submits together.
form.rtl: Labels, fields and errors align to the start.

form_field.headline: Label, hint and error, always in place.
form_field.intro: Wraps any input with its label, description and error, wired for screen readers.
form_field.what: A field wrapper with label, description and error.
form_field.when: Use it around custom inputs that need the standard frame.
form_field.rtl: Label and messages align to the start in both directions.

form_section.headline: Long forms, broken into clear steps.
form_section.intro: A titled group of fields with a description, so long forms read as a few short ones.
form_section.what: A titled group of fields in a form.
form_section.when: Use it to split long forms into meaningful parts.
form_section.rtl: Titles and fields align to the start.

foundations.headline: The tokens every screen is built on.
foundations.intro: Colours, contrast, radius and motion in one place, tuned per brand and checked for contrast in light and dark.
foundations.what: The colour, radius and motion tokens of the system.
foundations.when: Use it to look up a token before you style anything.
foundations.rtl: Tokens are direction-free; components apply them with logical properties.

fullscreen_bar.headline: Full focus, with a way out.
fullscreen_bar.intro: The exit and title bar of a full-screen POS, kitchen display, kiosk or editor, which hides until needed.
fullscreen_bar.what: The bar of a full-screen mode.
fullscreen_bar.when: Use it on POS, KDS, kiosk and editor screens.
fullscreen_bar.rtl: Exit sits at the start; actions at the end.

funnel_chart.headline: See exactly where people leave.
funnel_chart.intro: Teams know which step to fix first, not just that sales dropped.
funnel_chart.what: A chart of shrinking steps from first visit to purchase.
funnel_chart.when: Use it for checkout, signup and sales pipelines.
funnel_chart.rtl: Labels sit at the start and percentages keep their figures in Arabic digits when chosen.

holo_card.headline: A card worth showing off.
holo_card.intro: It calms down to a still card when people prefer less motion.
holo_card.when: Use it for loyalty tiers, gift cards and member passes.
holo_card.rtl: Text on the card aligns to the start; the shine follows the finger either way.

hover_card.headline: A preview without leaving the page.
hover_card.intro: The essentials show in place, so people keep their flow instead of opening tabs.
hover_card.what: A small card that previews what a link points to.
hover_card.when: Use it to give context to mentions, references and IDs.
hover_card.rtl: The card opens toward the end and its content aligns to the start.

icon.headline: One icon set, sized and named consistently.
icon.intro: Named icons in the system set with sizes, tones and automatic mirroring for directional shapes.
icon.what: A named icon from the system set.
icon.when: Use it for any icon so sizes and tones stay consistent.
icon.rtl: Directional icons such as arrows and chevrons mirror; logos and clocks never do.

icon_button.headline: Compact actions that still say what they do.
icon_button.intro: Square, icon-only buttons for toolbars and dense rows, each with a required accessible name and the same press feedback as Button.
icon_button.what: A button that shows only an icon.
icon_button.when: Use it in toolbars and tight rows where the icon is widely understood.
icon_button.rtl: Directional icons such as back and next mirror in Arabic.
icon_button.when_not: When the icon is not universally understood; add a label.
icon_button.do_1: Give every icon button an accessible name.
icon_button.do_2: Add a tooltip that repeats the name.
icon_button.dont_1: Do not invent icons for rare actions.
icon_button.dont_2: Do not shrink the target below 44 points.

alternative.button: When the action needs words to be clear.
alternative.close_button: For dismissing panels, dialogs and messages.

import_flow.headline: Import a spreadsheet with no surprises.
import_flow.intro: Nothing is written until people have seen exactly what will change.
import_flow.what: A step-by-step flow for bringing data in.
import_flow.when: Use it for catalogues, customer lists and price updates.
import_flow.rtl: Steps advance from the right in Arabic; column names keep their own direction.

inline_edit.headline: Fix a value without leaving the page.
inline_edit.intro: Click or tap to edit in place, then save or cancel, with the same validation as a full form.
inline_edit.what: A value that can be edited in place.
inline_edit.when: Use it for quick edits to single values on detail pages.
inline_edit.rtl: Save and cancel sit at the end; the value keeps its own direction.

inline_loading.headline: Show progress right where it happens.
inline_loading.intro: A small spinner that turns into a success or error message in place, announced to screen readers.
inline_loading.what: An inline spinner that resolves to a result.
inline_loading.when: Use it next to a save or a sync that takes a moment.
inline_loading.rtl: The spinner leads at the start; the message follows.

inline_select.headline: A choice that reads like a sentence.
inline_select.intro: Filters and settings read as plain language, and stay compact.
inline_select.what: A select shown as a word in a sentence.
inline_select.when: Use it in filters and settings phrased as plain language.
inline_select.rtl: The sentence and its word follow Arabic order; the list opens from the start.

input_group.headline: Give every field the context it needs.
input_group.intro: A text field with leading or trailing add-ons such as units, prefixes and buttons.
input_group.when: Use it for URLs, units, currencies and inline actions.
input_group.rtl: Leading add-ons move to the right in Arabic; Latin prefixes such as https:// stay LTR.

item_card.headline: Rows that look as good as cards.
item_card.intro: Settings and menus look polished without building a custom row each time.
item_card.what: A card laid out like a list row.
item_card.when: Use it for settings, menus and short lists of things to open.
item_card.rtl: The icon leads at the start and the chevron points left in Arabic.

kpi.headline: The numbers that matter, at a glance.
kpi.intro: A team sees in one glance whether it is on track, and drills in when it is not.
kpi.what: A tile for one key figure.
kpi.when: Use it at the top of dashboards and reports.
kpi.rtl: Text aligns to the start; the trend arrow keeps its meaning and the sparkline runs from the right.

leave_confirmation.headline: Unsaved work stays safe.
leave_confirmation.intro: Asks before leaving a page with unsaved changes, in the app and on browser close.
leave_confirmation.what: A guard that asks before leaving.
leave_confirmation.when: Use it on forms and editors that do not autosave.
leave_confirmation.rtl: Dialog buttons follow the reading order.

line_chart.headline: Follow every trend without the noise.
line_chart.intro: Clean lines with optional dots, a dashed hover guide and a ringed active point that stays legible on any surface.
line_chart.tags: Trends · Multi-series · Annotations · Log scale · Synced
line_chart.what: A chart of one or more trends as lines, with target lines, notes pinned to dates, a log axis and crosshairs shared across charts.
line_chart.when: Use it to show change over time and compare a few series.
line_chart.rtl: Time runs from right to left in Arabic; the tooltip opens toward the inside.

link.headline: Go anywhere, with clear intent.
link.intro: An accessible link with external and download hints, styled to read as a link everywhere.
link.what: A link to another page or place.
link.when: Use it to navigate; use a button to act.
link.rtl: External arrows mirror; URLs inside text are isolated.
link.when_not: To run an action; use a button.
link.do_1: Write link text that says where it goes.
link.do_2: Mark links that leave the product.
link.dont_2: Do not style buttons as links or links as buttons.

alternative.button: When the press does something instead of going somewhere.

list.headline: Clean lists that scale from three items to thousands.
list.intro: A vertical list with optional selection, keyboard movement and start and end slots for icons and actions. With virtual scrolling it draws only the rows in view, for ten thousand and more.
list.when: Use it for simple collections where a table is too much.
list.rtl: Start content leads from the right in Arabic; trailing chevrons mirror.

locale_switcher.headline: Every language, in its own words.
locale_switcher.intro: Anyone can find their language, even when the app is in one they cannot read.
locale_switcher.what: A control for the app's language.
locale_switcher.when: Use it in headers, settings and onboarding.
locale_switcher.rtl: Choosing Arabic flips the whole layout; each name keeps its own script.

menu.headline: Options in a neat, keyboard-first list.
menu.intro: A popover list of actions or options with sections, icons, shortcuts and checkable items.
menu.what: A list of actions or options in a popover.
menu.when: Use it behind a button for actions or choices.
menu.rtl: Shortcuts sit at the end; submenus open toward the end.
menu.when_not: For choosing a form value; use a select.
menu.do_2: Put destructive actions last, in danger tone.
menu.dont_1: Do not hide the only way to do a common task.
menu.dont_2: Do not nest more than one submenu.

alternative.action_menu: For a ready-made trigger and actions.

modal.headline: Focus on one task, then return.
modal.intro: A dialog above the page that holds focus, closes on Escape and returns focus where it came from.
modal.when: Use it for short tasks that need full attention.
modal.rtl: Content aligns to the start; the close button sits at the end.
modal.when_not: For long tasks or anything people need to compare with the page; use a drawer or a page.
modal.do_1: Give it a clear title and one primary action.
modal.do_2: Return focus to the trigger on close.
modal.do_3: Use a modal when people enter or edit something: "Rename project" with a name field, Save and Cancel.
modal.dont_2: Do not open a modal on page load.
modal.dont_3: Do not use a modal for a yes-or-no question such as "Delete this file?"; that is an alert dialog.

alternative.drawer: When the page should stay visible.

mode_switch.headline: Switch views with one tap.
mode_switch.intro: A segmented control for a few modes, such as list and grid, with a sliding indicator.
mode_switch.what: A control that switches between a few modes.
mode_switch.when: Use it for two to four mutually exclusive views.
mode_switch.rtl: Segments follow the reading order; the indicator slides the mirrored way.

money_field.headline: Amounts that are always right.
money_field.intro: A currency-aware amount field with minor units and locale digits, so 1,234.50 and ١٬٢٣٤٫٥٠ both work.
money_field.what: An amount field with currency and minor units.
money_field.when: Use it for prices, payments and budgets.
money_field.rtl: The amount is isolated; the currency sits where the locale expects it.

morph_button.headline: One button, the whole story.
morph_button.intro: One button narrows to a spinner, turns into a green check when it's done, or shakes and asks to try again.
morph_button.what: A button that changes shape with its action's state.
morph_button.when: Use it for saves and payments where people wait for an outcome.
morph_button.rtl: In Arabic the words and marks follow the reading direction; the morph runs the same.

morph_tabs.headline: Icons that grow into words.
morph_tabs.intro: The bar stays compact while the current place is always named.
morph_tabs.what: A tab bar whose active tab shows its label.
morph_tabs.when: Use it for bottom navigation with four or five destinations.
morph_tabs.rtl: Tabs run from the right in Arabic and the pill grows toward the end.

multi_select.headline: Pick many, see them all.
multi_select.intro: A filterable multi-pick that shows choices as removable chips and fits long lists.
multi_select.when: Use it to choose several items from a long list.
multi_select.rtl: Chips fill from the start; the trigger sits at the end.

native_select.headline: The chooser your device already knows.
native_select.intro: People get the chooser they already know, with nothing new to learn.
native_select.what: A select that uses the system picker.
native_select.when: Use it on mobile forms where the system picker feels most natural.
native_select.rtl: The system picker follows the device language and direction.

navigation_header.headline: Back and title, where people expect them.
navigation_header.intro: A screen header with back, title and actions that matches native conventions.
navigation_header.rtl: Back sits at the start and its arrow mirrors.

navigation_list.headline: Every section of the app, one tap away.
navigation_list.intro: A list of links to the sections of an app, with icons, badges and the current page marked.
navigation_list.what: A list of links to app sections.
navigation_list.when: Use it for settings menus and section indexes.
navigation_list.rtl: Chevrons mirror; icons lead at the start.

notifications_panel.headline: Everything new, in one calm inbox.
notifications_panel.intro: Grouped notifications with unread state, mark all read and quick actions, on web and mobile alike.
notifications_panel.when: Use it behind the bell in the app header.
notifications_panel.rtl: Groups and times read in Arabic; relative times use Arabic plurals.

number_field.headline: Type it or step it, either way it is valid.
number_field.intro: A number field with steppers, limits and locale formatting that stays keyboard friendly.
number_field.what: A field for typing and stepping numbers.
number_field.when: Use it for quantities and bounded numbers.
number_field.rtl: Steppers stay put; the number keeps its digits and direction.
number_field.when_not: For IDs, phone numbers and codes that are not quantities.
number_field.do_1: Set a minimum, maximum and step.
number_field.dont_1: Do not use it for phone numbers.
number_field.dont_2: Do not hide the steppers on touch.

number_pad.headline: Amounts and PINs without the keyboard.
number_pad.intro: Large keys and a light buzz on every tap make entry fast and sure.
number_pad.when: Use it for payments, cash counts and PIN entry.
number_pad.rtl: The keypad keeps its phone layout in Arabic, so every digit sits where the thumb expects it.

number_ticker.headline: Numbers that arrive with a little life.
number_ticker.intro: It draws the eye to the figure that matters, and simply appears when motion is off.
number_ticker.when: Use it on dashboards and landing pages to draw the eye to a key figure.
number_ticker.rtl: It counts in Arabic-Indic digits when the locale uses them.

otp_input.headline: Codes that fill themselves in.
otp_input.intro: Codes fill themselves in from the message, so verification takes a second.
otp_input.what: A field for a one-time code.
otp_input.when: Use it for sign-in, payment and phone checks.
otp_input.rtl: Boxes run left to right like the code itself, also in Arabic.

overflow_list.headline: Show the first few, count the rest.
overflow_list.intro: Chips line up until space runs out, then fold into a +N more that opens the full list.
overflow_list.what: A list that folds extra items into +N more.
overflow_list.when: Use it for tags and assignees in table cells and cards.
overflow_list.rtl: Items fill from the start; the +N sits at the end.

overflow_toolbar.headline: Every action stays reachable, at any width.
overflow_toolbar.intro: Actions line up in a row and fold into a More menu as space runs out, so nothing disappears on a phone.
overflow_toolbar.what: A toolbar that moves what does not fit into a More menu.
overflow_toolbar.when: Use it above editors, records and tables with more actions than room.
overflow_toolbar.rtl: The row fills from the start edge and the More menu sits at the end.

page_header.headline: Every page opens with a clear purpose.
page_header.intro: Title, description, breadcrumbs and actions at the top of a page, consistent across products.
page_header.when: Use it at the top of every page.
page_header.rtl: Title at the start, actions at the end.

page_skeleton.headline: A page that feels fast before it is ready.
page_skeleton.intro: A placeholder layout in the page's real shape, so content slots in without a jump.
page_skeleton.what: A placeholder layout while a page loads.
page_skeleton.when: Use it for the first load of a full page.
page_skeleton.rtl: The placeholder mirrors with the layout it stands for.

password_field.headline: Secure entry, without the guesswork.
password_field.intro: A masked field with a reveal toggle and a PIN mode, labelled for password managers and screen readers.
password_field.what: A masked field with a reveal toggle.
password_field.when: Use it for passwords, PINs and secrets.
password_field.rtl: The reveal button sits at the end; passwords stay left to right.

permissions_matrix.headline: See and set who can do what.
permissions_matrix.intro: A role-by-permission grid with grouped bulk toggles and an access summary per role, built for real admin work.
permissions_matrix.when: Use it in admin settings to manage roles and their rights.
permissions_matrix.rtl: Permission names read from the right; role columns follow the reading order.

phone_field.headline: Every number, ready to dial.
phone_field.intro: Numbers are checked as people type, so messages reach the right phone.
phone_field.what: One field: the flag opens a searchable list of countries, then you type the number.
phone_field.when: Use it at sign-up, checkout and contact forms.
phone_field.rtl: The number stays left to right; the country button sits at the start, on the right in Arabic.

pie_chart.headline: Each part's share, made obvious.
pie_chart.intro: A simple pie for a few parts of one whole, with a legend that names every slice for screen readers too.
pie_chart.what: A chart of each part's share of a whole.
pie_chart.when: Use it for two to five parts; beyond that, prefer a bar chart.
pie_chart.rtl: Slices follow the reading direction; the legend aligns to the start.

popover.headline: Extra detail, right beside the trigger.
popover.intro: Floating content anchored to a trigger that repositions to stay on screen.
popover.what: Floating content anchored to a trigger.
popover.when: Use it for small forms, pickers and rich hints.
popover.rtl: Placement flips with direction: start and end, not left and right.
popover.when_not: For essential information; put it on the page.
popover.do_1: Anchor it to the element it explains.
popover.do_2: Close it on Escape and outside press.
popover.dont_1: Do not put long forms inside.
popover.dont_2: Do not open it on hover only.

alternative.modal: For a task that needs full attention.

popover.do_3: Call updatePosition from usePopoverPosition when the trigger moves without changing size; growing content re-anchors on its own.

press_feedback.headline: Every touch gets an answer.
press_feedback.intro: Custom tiles feel as responsive as the system's own buttons.
press_feedback.what: A wrapper that shows and feels a press.
press_feedback.when: Use it for custom tappable cards and tiles.
press_feedback.rtl: The press looks and feels the same in either direction.

progress_bar.headline: Show how far, and how much is left.
progress_bar.intro: A line that fills as a task moves, with an optional label and value, or an indeterminate sweep.
progress_bar.what: A line that shows a task's progress.
progress_bar.when: Use it for uploads, imports and multi-step tasks.
progress_bar.rtl: The fill grows from the right in Arabic.
progress_bar.when_not: For short waits; use a spinner.
progress_bar.do_1: Show the value when it is known.
progress_bar.dont_1: Do not move the bar backward.
progress_bar.dont_2: Do not show 100% before the task is done.

progress_button.headline: Watch it finish.
progress_button.intro: People see it is working and how far it got, so nobody presses twice.
progress_button.what: A button with a progress fill.
progress_button.when: Use it for uploads, exports and longer saves.
progress_button.rtl: The fill grows from the right in Arabic.

progress_circle.headline: Progress that fits anywhere.
progress_circle.intro: A ring that fills around its value, compact enough for buttons, cards and tiles.
progress_circle.what: A ring that shows a task's progress.
progress_circle.when: Use it where a bar does not fit, such as a tile or a button.
progress_circle.rtl: The ring fills in the reading direction.

property_list.headline: Every detail of a record, easy to scan.
property_list.intro: Label and value pairs in one or two columns that stay aligned, with copy actions for IDs and codes.
property_list.what: Label and value pairs describing a record.
property_list.when: Use it on detail pages and side panels.
property_list.rtl: Labels sit at the start; Latin values such as IDs are isolated.

pull_to_refresh.headline: Fresh data, one pull away.
pull_to_refresh.intro: A spinner follows the pull and the wait, so people know fresh data is on its way.
pull_to_refresh.what: A list that reloads when pulled down.
pull_to_refresh.when: Use it for feeds, orders and inboxes on mobile.
pull_to_refresh.rtl: The pull works the same in either direction.

quantity_stepper.headline: Change the count without typing.
quantity_stepper.intro: Limits are respected and removing a line takes one tap.
quantity_stepper.what: A small control to raise or lower a count.
quantity_stepper.when: Use it in carts, orders and stock adjustments.
quantity_stepper.rtl: Minus and plus swap sides in Arabic; the count keeps its digits.

radar_chart.headline: Compare profiles across many measures.
radar_chart.intro: Series drawn on spokes reveal strengths and gaps across several measures in one shape.
radar_chart.what: A chart that compares series on spokes.
radar_chart.when: Use it to compare two or three profiles over five to eight measures.
radar_chart.rtl: Spokes keep their order; labels sit outside and read in Arabic.

radial_bar_chart.headline: Progress toward every goal, in rings.
radial_bar_chart.intro: Rings fill to their values on soft tracks, so several goals read at a glance in a small space.
radial_bar_chart.what: A chart of rings filled to their values.
radial_bar_chart.when: Use it for progress toward a few goals, such as targets per team.
radial_bar_chart.rtl: Rings fill in the reading direction; labels align to the start.

radio_button_group.headline: One choice, with all the facts.
radio_button_group.intro: A title and a line of detail on each card let people choose with confidence.
radio_button_group.what: A group of cards where only one can be chosen.
radio_button_group.when: Use it for plans, delivery methods and payment options.
radio_button_group.rtl: Cards flow from the start and the radio sits at the start edge.

radio_group.headline: One choice, all options in view.
radio_group.intro: A labelled set of options where only one can be chosen, with arrow-key movement.
radio_group.what: A set of options with one choice.
radio_group.when: Use it for two to five options people should compare.
radio_group.rtl: Arrow keys follow the reading direction; radios lead each label.
radio_group.when_not: For more than seven options; use a select.
radio_group.dont_1: Do not use a single radio button.
radio_group.dont_2: Do not change other fields silently when one is picked.

alternative.select: For many options in little space.

range_calendar.headline: A whole period on one month view.
range_calendar.intro: Bookings, leave and report periods are marked in two taps.
range_calendar.what: A calendar for picking a range of days.
range_calendar.when: Use it inline for bookings, leave and report periods.
range_calendar.rtl: Weeks run from the right; previous and next arrows mirror.

range_slider.headline: Set the low and the high in one move.
range_slider.intro: Values show while dragging, and the keyboard can set each end exactly.
range_slider.when: Use it for price filters, age ranges and quantities.
range_slider.rtl: The track runs from the right in Arabic, so low starts on the right.

reaction_button.headline: Say it with one tap.
reaction_button.intro: A little pop on each tap makes feedback feel friendly, not formal.
reaction_button.what: A toggle that shows a reaction and its count, and adds your own tap to it.
reaction_button.when: Use it on comments, posts and updates.
reaction_button.rtl: The emoji leads at the start and the count follows.

reveal.headline: Content that arrives with intent.
reveal.intro: Animates content into view as it appears, and stays still when people ask for reduced motion.
reveal.what: A wrapper that animates content into view.
reveal.when: Use it for hero sections and content that loads in.
reveal.rtl: Slides start from the start edge, so they mirror in Arabic.

route_overlay.headline: Open details without losing the list.
route_overlay.intro: Opens a route as a modal or drawer over the page, so links, back and refresh all work.
route_overlay.what: A route opened as an overlay.
route_overlay.when: Use it for record details opened from a list.
route_overlay.rtl: Drawers open from the end edge; back restores the list.

route_progress.headline: Navigation that never feels stuck.
route_progress.intro: A thin bar across the top while the next page loads, so every click gets instant feedback.
route_progress.what: A thin loading bar for route changes.
route_progress.when: Use it once, in the app shell.
route_progress.rtl: The bar grows from the start edge.

rule_builder.headline: Rules in plain words, no code.
rule_builder.intro: Teams shape automations and segments themselves, without waiting for a developer.
rule_builder.what: An editor for conditions and groups.
rule_builder.when: Use it for automations, segments and filters people define themselves.
rule_builder.rtl: The sentence reads from the right in Arabic; nested groups indent toward the end.

save_bar.headline: Never lose a change again.
save_bar.intro: A sticky bar that appears with unsaved changes and offers save or discard, with an autosave status when on.
save_bar.what: A bar to save or discard changes.
save_bar.when: Use it on forms and settings that save as a whole.
save_bar.rtl: Status reads at the start; save and discard sit at the end.

screen.headline: A screen body that respects every edge.
screen.intro: A scrollable body with safe areas and the page gutter built in.
screen.what: The scrollable body of a screen.
screen.when: Use it as the body of every screen.
screen.rtl: Padding uses logical sides, so it mirrors with the layout.

search_field.headline: Find it as you type.
search_field.intro: A search field with a clear button, Enter to submit and Escape to clear.
search_field.when: Use it above lists, tables and in headers.
search_field.rtl: The search icon leads at the start; the clear button sits at the end.
search_field.when_not: To pick a value from a fixed list; use a combo box.
search_field.do_1: Show results as people type, when fast.
search_field.do_2: Keep the query after results load.
search_field.dont_1: Do not hide the clear button.
search_field.dont_2: Do not search on every key for slow sources.

alternative.combo_box: When the search picks one value.
alternative.filter_bar: When people also narrow by fields.

section.headline: Pages that read in clear blocks.
section.intro: A titled block with description and actions, so long pages scan as a list of sections.
section.what: A titled block on a page.
section.when: Use it to group related content on a page.
section.rtl: Title at the start, actions at the end.

segmented_control.headline: Switch views in one tap.
segmented_control.intro: The sliding thumb shows the current view at a glance.
segmented_control.when: Use it to switch between two to five views of the same thing.
segmented_control.rtl: Segments run from the right in Arabic and the thumb slides with them.

select.headline: Pick one, from a tidy list.
select.intro: A trigger that opens a list of options in a popover, with sections and a native sheet on mobile.
select.what: Picks one option from a list.
select.when: Use it for six or more options where space is tight.
select.rtl: The value aligns to the start; the indicator sits at the end.
select.when_not: For two to five options people should compare; use radios.
select.do_1: Sort options in a predictable order.
select.dont_1: Do not use it for yes or no.
select.dont_2: Do not put actions inside the options.

alternative.radio_group: When all options should be visible.
alternative.combo_box: When the list is long enough to search.
alternative.multi_select: When several options can be picked.

separator.headline: Quiet lines that organise.
separator.intro: A horizontal or vertical divider in the theme's separator colour, hidden from screen readers when decorative.
separator.when: Use it between groups that need a light boundary.
separator.rtl: Vertical separators follow the reading order.

setting_row.headline: Settings people understand at a glance.
setting_row.intro: One setting with its title, description and a switch or action, laid out the same everywhere.
setting_row.when: Use it on settings pages, one row per choice.
setting_row.rtl: Title and description at the start; the control at the end.

settings_cell.headline: Every setting, one tidy row.
settings_cell.intro: Rows stack into a full settings screen that looks consistent everywhere.
settings_cell.what: A row that holds one setting.
settings_cell.when: Use it to build settings and preferences screens.
settings_cell.rtl: The label leads at the start and the control sits at the end.

setup_guide.headline: Guide every new customer to their first win.
setup_guide.intro: An onboarding checklist with progress that celebrates each step and folds away once everything is done.
setup_guide.when: Use it on the home of a new account.
setup_guide.rtl: Steps read from the start; the progress fills from the right in Arabic.

sidebar.headline: Navigation that stays out of the way.
sidebar.intro: A side panel of navigation that collapses to icons and becomes a drawer on a phone.
sidebar.when: Use it for apps with many sections.
sidebar.rtl: It sits at the start edge, so it moves to the right in Arabic; the active bar, the rail's dots and the sub-menu guide follow, and the toggle's icon turns.
sidebar.when_not: For a few top-level places on a phone; use a tab bar.
sidebar.do_1: Mark the place the user is on, and keep each label short enough to read in one glance.
sidebar.do_2: Give every top-level place an icon, so the collapsed rail still reads.
sidebar.dont_1: Do not nest deeper than one sub-menu; split the section instead.
sidebar.dont_2: Do not hide the only way back: an offcanvas sidebar needs a trigger in the page header.

alternative.app_shell: The page frame that holds a sidebar and a header, with its own drawer.
alternative.navigation_list: The same places as a plain list, for a settings page.
alternative.tabs: For a few views of one place.

side_panel.headline: Room for a second task, without covering the first.
side_panel.intro: A panel at the end of the page that pushes the content aside, resizes from its border and expands to take the whole area.
side_panel.what: A panel column that is part of the page: closed, open or expanded.
side_panel.when: Use it for work beside the page: an assistant, an inspector, comments.
side_panel.rtl: It sits at the end edge, so it moves to the left in Arabic; its border handle and the arrow keys follow, and the launcher stays centred.
side_panel.when_not: For a short task that should block the page; use a drawer.
side_panel.do_1: Keep the page usable beside it: pick a width that leaves the content readable.
side_panel.do_2: Give the panel a name, so its landmark is announced.
side_panel.dont_1: Do not open it on its own while the user is working in the page.
side_panel.dont_2: Do not nest a second side panel inside it.

alternative.sidebar: Navigation at the start edge that collapses to icons.
alternative.drawer: A temporary task over the page, behind a scrim.
alternative.app_shell: The page frame; a side panel goes inside its content.

single_column_layout.headline: One column, full attention.
single_column_layout.intro: A centred column at a comfortable reading width for focused pages such as sign-in and checkout.
single_column_layout.when: Use it for focused flows and forms.
single_column_layout.rtl: Centred, so it reads the same in both directions.

skeleton.headline: Loading that looks like the content.
skeleton.intro: Placeholder shapes in the size of what is coming, with a shimmer that stops for reduced motion.
skeleton.what: A placeholder shape while content loads.
skeleton.when: Use it for cards, rows and text that load in place.

slide_to_confirm.headline: Deliberate actions, never by accident.
slide_to_confirm.intro: Weighty actions never happen by accident, and the keyboard has its own path.
slide_to_confirm.what: A track you slide across to confirm.
slide_to_confirm.when: Use it for payments, deletions and handovers that should not happen by mistake.
slide_to_confirm.rtl: The thumb slides from right to left in Arabic.

social_sign_in_buttons.headline: Sign in the way you already do.
social_sign_in_buttons.intro: Each button follows its provider's rules, so sign-in feels familiar and trusted.
social_sign_in_buttons.what: A set of sign-in buttons, one per provider.
social_sign_in_buttons.when: Use it on sign-in and sign-up screens.
social_sign_in_buttons.rtl: Logos lead at the start; provider names keep their own spelling.

sortable_list.headline: Reorder by drag, keys or voice.
sortable_list.intro: Rows reorder by dragging, by keyboard or with a screen reader, with clear announcements of every move.
sortable_list.what: A list whose rows can be reordered.
sortable_list.when: Use it for priorities, menus and steps people arrange.
sortable_list.rtl: The drag handle sits at the start edge in both directions.

sparkline.headline: A trend that fits in a sentence.
sparkline.intro: A word-sized line for table cells and stat tiles that shows direction without axes or chrome.
sparkline.what: A tiny trend line without axes.
sparkline.when: Use it inside tables, lists and KPI tiles next to the number.
sparkline.rtl: Time runs from right to left in Arabic, matching the larger charts.

spinner.headline: A short wait, clearly signalled.
spinner.intro: A themed spinner with an accessible label for waits too short to measure.
spinner.what: An indicator that something is loading.
spinner.when: Use it for short, unmeasured waits.
spinner.rtl: The spinner is symmetric; its label follows the reading direction.
spinner.when_not: For waits longer than a few seconds; show progress.
spinner.do_2: Show it only after a short delay.
spinner.dont_1: Do not use several spinners on one screen.
spinner.dont_2: Do not block the whole page for a small update.

alternative.skeleton: When the content's shape is known.
alternative.inline_loading: When the result should replace it in place.

split_button.headline: The likely action first, the rest one tap away.
split_button.intro: A primary button joined to a caret menu of related actions, so the common path stays fast and the options stay close.
split_button.what: A primary action joined to a menu of related actions.
split_button.when: Use it when one action is most likely and a few close variants exist.
split_button.rtl: The caret moves to the start-facing end in Arabic; the menu aligns to it.

split_view.headline: The list and its detail, together.
split_view.intro: People keep the list in view while they read, so moving to the next item takes one tap.
split_view.what: A layout of a list and its detail.
split_view.when: Use it for inboxes, orders and catalogues.
split_view.rtl: The list sits on the right in Arabic and the detail on the left.

stacked_meter.headline: One bar, everything that fills it.
stacked_meter.intro: People see at once what is using their limit, before they run out.
stacked_meter.what: A bar split into coloured parts.
stacked_meter.when: Use it to show what uses up a limit.
stacked_meter.rtl: Segments fill from the right in Arabic and the legend follows.

status_badge.headline: Every record's status, at a glance.
status_badge.intro: A coloured label with a dot for statuses such as paid, pending or failed, mapped once and reused everywhere.
status_badge.what: A coloured label for a record's status.
status_badge.when: Use it in tables, cards and detail headers.
status_badge.rtl: The dot leads at the start of the label.
status_badge.do_1: Map each status to one tone everywhere.
status_badge.dont_1: Do not invent new tones per page.
status_badge.dont_2: Do not use it for actions.

alternative.status_indicator: For live states with a shape.

status_indicator.headline: States everyone can read, not only by colour.
status_indicator.intro: Colour, shape and icon together, so status survives colour blindness, grayscale and print.
status_indicator.what: A state shown by colour, shape and icon.
status_indicator.when: Use it for live states such as online, busy or offline.
status_indicator.rtl: The indicator leads at the start of its label.

surface.headline: Layers that give depth without noise.
surface.intro: Themed background layers that set colour and contrast for everything placed on them.
surface.when: Use it to separate regions such as panels and wells.
surface.rtl: Direction-free; content inside follows the layout.

swipeable_row.headline: Act on a row with a swipe.
swipeable_row.intro: A full swipe runs the main action, so inboxes clear in seconds.
swipeable_row.what: A list row with hidden actions.
swipeable_row.when: Use it in inboxes and lists on mobile.
swipeable_row.rtl: Swipe directions mirror in Arabic, so start and end actions keep their meaning.

swipeable_tabs.headline: Swipe between sections naturally.
swipeable_tabs.intro: The indicator follows the finger, so moving between sections feels natural.
swipeable_tabs.when: Use it for sections of one screen that people browse in turn.
swipeable_tabs.rtl: Tabs run from the right and the swipe follows Arabic order.

switch.headline: On or off, right away.
switch.intro: A switch for settings that apply instantly, with a thumb that slides and a haptic on mobile.
switch.what: Turns a setting on or off immediately.
switch.when: Use it for settings that take effect without a save.
switch.rtl: The thumb slides toward the end when on, so it moves left in Arabic.
switch.when_not: When the change waits for a save; use a checkbox.
switch.do_2: Label the setting, not the state.
switch.dont_1: Do not ask for confirmation for every toggle.
switch.dont_2: Do not use on and off as the label.

alternative.setting_row: For a full settings row with a description.

system_banner.headline: Tell everyone, once, at the top.
system_banner.intro: An app-wide message for outages, trials and announcements that people can dismiss, stacked two at most.
system_banner.when: Use it for news that affects the whole account.
system_banner.rtl: The message reads from the start; the close button sits at the end.

table.headline: Rows and columns, done right.
table.intro: A plain, accessible table with sticky headers and aligned numbers for when you need data, not features.
table.when: Use it for static or small data sets without sorting or selection.
table.rtl: Columns start from the right in Arabic; numeric columns align to the end.

tabs.headline: Switch views without losing your place.
tabs.intro: Tabs with a sliding indicator, full arrow-key support and panels that keep their state. Tabs can close, and the ones that do not fit can move into a More menu.
tabs.what: Switches between views in one place.
tabs.when: Use it for peer views of the same thing.
tabs.rtl: Tabs start from the right in Arabic and arrow keys follow.
tabs.when_not: For steps in a sequence; use a stepper.
tabs.do_1: Keep tab labels short and parallel.
tabs.do_2: Keep each panel's state when switching.
tabs.dont_1: Do not nest tabs inside tabs.
tabs.dont_2: Do not use tabs to hide required fields.

alternative.mode_switch: For switching how one view is shown.
alternative.accordion: When people need several sections open at once.

tag_group.headline: Tags people can pick and prune.
tag_group.intro: A group of tags that can be selected or removed, with full keyboard support.
tag_group.what: A group of selectable or removable tags.
tag_group.when: Use it for filters and labels on a record.
tag_group.rtl: Tags fill from the start; remove buttons sit at each tag's end.

text_area.headline: Room to write, that grows with you.
text_area.intro: A multi-line field that grows with its content, with an optional counter and the same states as Text field.
text_area.what: A field for several lines of text.
text_area.when: Use it for notes, messages and descriptions.
text_area.rtl: Text direction follows what people type, so mixed notes read right.
text_area.do_1: Size it to the expected length of the text.
text_area.do_2: Show a counter when there is a limit.
text_area.dont_1: Do not use it for short values.
text_area.dont_2: Do not cut text without warning.

text_field.headline: The field people fill without thinking.
text_field.intro: Label, input, description and error in one accessible field, with clear focus and validation states.
text_field.what: A field for one line of text.
text_field.when: Use it for names, emails and any short text.
text_field.rtl: Labels align to the start; email and URL inputs stay left to right.
text_field.when_not: For several lines of text or for numbers.
text_field.do_1: Keep a visible label on every field.
text_field.do_2: Explain errors and how to fix them.
text_field.dont_1: Do not use the placeholder as the label.
text_field.dont_2: Do not validate while people are still typing the first time.

alternative.number_field: For numbers with limits and steps.
alternative.search_field: For search with a clear button.

text_reveal.headline: Headlines that arrive with presence.
text_reveal.intro: Headlines arrive with presence, and simply appear when motion is reduced.
text_reveal.what: A headline that reveals its words in turn.
text_reveal.when: Use it for hero sections and onboarding titles.
text_reveal.rtl: Arabic reveals word by word, never letter by letter, so letters stay joined.

thumbnail.headline: Images that load gracefully.
thumbnail.intro: A fixed aspect ratio, a blur-up placeholder and an icon fallback, so layouts never jump and broken images never show.
thumbnail.what: A resource's image with placeholder and fallback.
thumbnail.when: Use it for products, files and media in lists and cards.
thumbnail.rtl: Images never mirror; badges on them follow the end corner.

time_field.headline: Times, typed or chosen.
time_field.intro: It respects each locale's clock and digits.
time_field.what: A field for a time of day.
time_field.when: Use it in schedules, bookings and opening hours.
time_field.rtl: The time follows the locale's format and digits.

time_picker.headline: Set the time without typing.
time_picker.intro: A scrolling wheel sets the time without the keyboard.
time_picker.what: A time field with a wheel picker.
time_picker.when: Use it on mobile for appointments and reminders.
time_picker.rtl: The wheels follow the locale's order and the button sits at the end.

toast.headline: Confirm it, then get out of the way.
toast.intro: Short messages that slide in, stack and leave on their own, with an action and a pause on hover or focus. One toast can follow a save from spinner to result, and an undo toast counts down before the change is kept.
toast.what: A short message that disappears on its own.
toast.when: Use it to confirm an action that just happened.
toast.rtl: Toasts enter from the start edge and mirror in Arabic: the icon at the start, the dismiss button at the end.
toast.when_not: For errors people must act on; use an alert.
toast.do_1: Confirm the action in a few words.
toast.do_2: Offer Undo when it is possible.
toast.dont_1: Do not stack more than three.
toast.dont_2: Do not put critical information only in a toast.

alternative.alert: For messages tied to a page.

task_tray.headline: Long jobs, out of the way.
task_tray.intro: People keep working while uploads, exports and imports run. The tray shows how far each one is, says when one finishes or fails, and lets them cancel or try again.
task_tray.what: A docked card listing background tasks with their progress and state.
task_tray.when: For uploads, exports, imports and any job that outlasts a click.
task_tray.rtl: The tray docks in the bottom-left corner in Arabic, and each row reads from the right.
task_tray.when_not: For a job people must wait for; show progress in place instead.
task_tray.do_1: Name each task by what it makes, such as the file name.
task_tray.do_2: Keep failed tasks until they are retried or removed.
task_tray.dont_1: Do not open it for jobs that finish in a second.
task_tray.dont_2: Do not hide the reason a task failed.

alternative.toast: For one result that needs no follow-up.

recurrence_editor.headline: Say how often, in plain words.
recurrence_editor.intro: People set up a repeating meeting, delivery or reminder with a few controls and read the rule back in one sentence. Rules can count months in the Hijri calendar, so the first of Ramadan stays the first of Ramadan.
recurrence_editor.what: Controls that build an RFC 5545 repeating rule, with a summary.
recurrence_editor.when: For recurring events, subscriptions, reports and reminders.
recurrence_editor.rtl: The weekdays start on Sunday for Arabic and run from the right; the summary reads in Arabic with the customer's digits.
recurrence_editor.when_not: For a single date; use a date picker.
recurrence_editor.do_1: Start from the event's first day.
recurrence_editor.do_2: Show the summary so people can check the rule.
recurrence_editor.dont_1: Do not offer every RRULE part; keep to what people ask for.
recurrence_editor.dont_2: Do not store the summary; store the rule.

alternative.calendar: To see dates on a month grid.

toc_rail.headline: Always know where you are.
toc_rail.intro: Long pages stay easy to scan, and any section is one click away.
toc_rail.what: A table of contents for the current page.
toc_rail.when: Use it on long docs, policies and settings pages.
toc_rail.rtl: The rail sits at the end side and its marker at the start edge of each link.

toggle_button.headline: On or off, at a glance.
toggle_button.intro: Formatting and view options show their state at a glance.
toggle_button.what: A button with a pressed state.
toggle_button.when: Use it for bold, italic, list and grid choices.
toggle_button.rtl: Grouped buttons run from the right in Arabic.

tooltip.headline: A hint exactly when it helps.
tooltip.intro: A short label on hover or focus, delayed just enough to stay out of the way.
tooltip.what: A short hint on hover or focus.
tooltip.when: Use it to name icon buttons and explain truncated text.
tooltip.rtl: Placement uses start and end, so it flips with direction.
tooltip.when_not: For anything people must read to finish a task; show it on the page.
tooltip.do_1: Keep it to a few words.
tooltip.do_2: Use it to name icon-only buttons.
tooltip.dont_1: Do not put links or buttons inside.
tooltip.dont_2: Do not use it on disabled controls alone.

alternative.contextual_help: For a short explanation people open on purpose.

tree_view.headline: Navigate deep structures without getting lost.
tree_view.intro: Nested rows expand, collapse and select with full keyboard support and clear levels. Checkboxes can carry down to every row under a group, rows can load the first time their parent opens, and rows can be dragged to a new place.
tree_view.what: Nested rows that expand and collapse.
tree_view.when: Use it for folders, categories, permissions and org charts.
tree_view.rtl: Indentation grows from the start edge; chevrons mirror in Arabic.
tree_view.when_not: For choosing a value in a form; use a tree select.
tree_view.do_1: Load large branches on demand instead of all at once.
tree_view.do_2: Let a group's checkbox tick every row under it.
tree_view.dont_1: Do not nest more than four or five levels.
tree_view.dont_2: Do not make dragging the only way to move a row.

alternative.accordion: For a few sections of content.

tree_select.headline: A whole tree in one field.
tree_select.intro: People pick a category, an account or several branches from nested rows without leaving the form; ticking a region ticks its branches.
tree_select.what: A field whose options are a tree.
tree_select.when: Use it when the choices are nested: categories, chart of accounts, regions and branches.
tree_select.rtl: The trigger, the rows and their indentation start from the right in Arabic, and the chevrons mirror.
tree_select.when_not: For a flat list of options; use a select.
tree_select.do_1: Open the group that holds the current value.
tree_select.do_2: Keep row names short so the field can show them.
tree_select.dont_1: Do not hide the only rows people need under deep levels.
tree_select.dont_2: Do not use it for more than a few hundred rows without loading on demand.

alternative.select: For a flat list of options.
alternative.multi_select: For several options from a flat list.

masked_field.headline: The right format, as they type.
masked_field.intro: Mobile numbers, IBANs and card numbers take their spaces and separators as people type or paste, while the form receives only the characters.
masked_field.what: A text field that writes its value into a pattern.
masked_field.when: Use it for values with a fixed shape: phone numbers, IBANs, card numbers, dates and plates.
masked_field.rtl: The pattern reads left to right in Arabic too, sits at the field's start edge, and digits follow the digits setting.
masked_field.when_not: For free text or values of any length; use a text field.
masked_field.do_1: Show the pattern as the placeholder.
masked_field.do_2: Accept pasted values with or without separators.
masked_field.dont_1: Do not mask names or addresses.
masked_field.dont_2: Do not store the separators with the value.

alternative.phone_field: For phone numbers with a country.

mention_input.headline: Bring the right person in.
mention_input.intro: Typing @ suggests teammates by name; choosing one writes the name into the note, and the app learns who to notify.
mention_input.what: A text box that suggests people after @.
mention_input.when: Use it for comments, notes and messages that should reach someone.
mention_input.rtl: The list opens under the box from the right in Arabic, and Arabic and English names match as typed.
mention_input.when_not: For picking people into a field; use an entity picker.
mention_input.do_1: Show a face or initials beside each name.
mention_input.do_2: Tell people who will be notified.
mention_input.dont_1: Do not list everyone in the company at once.
mention_input.dont_2: Do not notify without showing the mention in the text.

alternative.tag_input: For a list of free-form tags.

treemap_chart.headline: Every share, sized to scale.
treemap_chart.intro: The biggest slices stand out instantly, and every tile names its share.
treemap_chart.what: A chart of nested rectangles sized by value.
treemap_chart.when: Use it for sales by category, spend by team and similar breakdowns.
treemap_chart.rtl: Tiles lay out from the right in Arabic.

two_column_layout.headline: Main work beside its context.
two_column_layout.intro: Main content with a side column that stacks below it on a phone.
two_column_layout.what: Main content beside a side column.
two_column_layout.when: Use it for detail pages with a summary or activity panel.
two_column_layout.rtl: The side column sits at the end, so it moves to the left in Arabic.

typography.headline: Type that reads beautifully in two scripts.
typography.intro: A shared type scale for headings and text, with Arabic and Latin faces paired and letter spacing off for Arabic.
typography.what: Headings and text in the system scale.
typography.when: Use it for every heading and paragraph.
typography.rtl: Arabic never gets letter spacing, so letters stay joined; alignment is start, not left.

use_breakpoint.headline: One answer to how big is this screen.
use_breakpoint.intro: A hook that returns the breakpoint and size class on web and native alike, so layouts branch the same way.
use_breakpoint.what: A hook for the screen's breakpoint.
use_breakpoint.when: Use it when a layout must change, not just restyle.

use_confirmation.headline: Confirm before acting, in one line of code.
use_confirmation.intro: A hook that asks for confirmation and resolves to yes or no, so any action can be guarded.
use_confirmation.what: A hook that asks for confirmation.
use_confirmation.when: Use it to guard destructive actions from any handler.
use_confirmation.rtl: The dialog it opens follows the reading order.

view_stack.headline: Go deeper, and back, without losing your place.
view_stack.intro: Drill into detail and back inside one panel, with the same motion on web and mobile.
view_stack.what: A panel that stacks views as you go deeper.
view_stack.when: Use it inside drawers, popovers and settings.
view_stack.rtl: New views enter from the left in Arabic and back points right.

visually_hidden.headline: Context for screen readers, silence for the eyes.
visually_hidden.intro: Text that assistive technology reads and the screen does not show, for labels the visual design already implies.
visually_hidden.what: Text read aloud but not shown.
visually_hidden.when: Use it to label icon-only controls and add context.
visually_hidden.rtl: Hidden text follows its parent's language and direction.

wheel_picker.headline: Spin, settle, done.
wheel_picker.intro: Wheels settle with a light buzz, which feels quicker than a long list.
wheel_picker.when: Use it on mobile where a wheel feels faster than a list.
wheel_picker.rtl: The wheels follow the locale's order.

widget_frame.headline: Every widget, calm in every state.
widget_frame.intro: Every dashboard card looks and behaves alike, even while loading or empty.
widget_frame.what: A frame around a dashboard widget.
widget_frame.when: Use it for every card on a dashboard so they look and behave alike.
widget_frame.rtl: The title leads at the start and actions sit at the end.

year_picker.headline: Jump straight to the year.
year_picker.intro: Birth years and fiscal years are one tap away, with no scrolling through months.
year_picker.what: A grid for choosing a year.
year_picker.when: Use it for birth years, fiscal years and archive filters.
year_picker.rtl: The grid fills from the right in Arabic.

import_dialog.headline: Bring data in, and know what changed.
