import_dialog.intro: Upload the file, match the columns and review a dry run before a single row is saved, then watch the import finish.
import_dialog.what: A step-by-step drawer for importing a spreadsheet.
import_dialog.when: Use it beside any table people fill from a file: customers, products, prices.
import_dialog.rtl: Steps and the drawer open from the reading side; column names keep their own direction.

slider.headline: One value, set by feel.
slider.intro: Drag to a value, step with the keys, or type it exactly. Marks show the common stops.
slider.what: A thumb on a track that sets one number.
slider.when: Use it when the range matters more than the exact figure: volume, discount, a budget.
slider.rtl: The track fills from the right in Arabic, and the arrow keys follow the reading direction.
slider.when_not: For an exact figure people already know; use a number field.
slider.do_1: Show the value beside the label, in the customer's digits.
slider.do_2: Add marks at the stops people pick most.
slider.dont_1: Do not use it for a range with two ends; use the range slider.
slider.dont_2: Do not hide the value only in the thumb.

alternative.range_slider: For a low and a high value.
alternative.number_field: For an exact number typed in.

pagination.headline: Every page, one press away.
pagination.intro: People see where they are, how much there is, and reach any page directly, at the size they prefer.
pagination.what: Numbered pages with previous, next and a summary.
pagination.when: Use it under a table or list whose total is known.
pagination.rtl: Pages run from the right in Arabic, and previous points right.
pagination.when_not: When the total is unknown or the feed is endless; use cursor pagination.
pagination.do_1: Show the summary so people know how much there is.
pagination.do_2: Offer page sizes that suit the screen.
pagination.dont_1: Do not show every page number of a long list.
pagination.dont_2: Do not reset the page when only a filter's order changes.

alternative.cursor_pagination: For an unknown total or a load-more list.

calendar.headline: The whole month, in view.
calendar.intro: People see open and closed days at a glance and pick one without opening anything.
calendar.what: A month grid for picking one day.
calendar.when: Use it when the day is the main choice on the screen: bookings, deliveries, appointments.
calendar.rtl: The week starts on the right in Arabic, and the month arrows mirror.
calendar.when_not: Inside a dense form; use the date picker, which opens the grid on demand.
calendar.do_1: Refuse closed days so people cannot pick them.
calendar.do_2: Offer the Hijri calendar where people plan by it.
calendar.dont_1: Do not use it for a range of days; use the range calendar.
calendar.dont_2: Do not use it for a birth date far in the past.

alternative.date_picker: For a day field inside a form.
alternative.range_calendar: For a start and an end day.

tag_input.headline: Type it, paste it, tag it.
tag_input.intro: People add tags as fast as they think, paste whole lists, and see straight away why one was refused.
tag_input.what: A field that turns typed text into removable tags.
tag_input.when: Use it for free-form labels, keywords and lists of addresses.
tag_input.rtl: Tags flow from the right in Arabic, keep their letters joined, and split on the Arabic comma too.
tag_input.when_not: When people choose from a known list; use a multi-select.
tag_input.do_1: Say why a tag was refused, next to the field.
tag_input.do_2: Show the count when there is a limit.
tag_input.dont_1: Do not silently drop pasted tags.
tag_input.dont_2: Do not use it for one value.

alternative.multi_select: For choosing from a known list.

timeline.headline: Every change, in the order it happened.
timeline.intro: People see who did what and when, by day, and follow a record's story without digging.
timeline.what: An activity feed of entries grouped by day.
timeline.when: Use it for order history, audit logs and a record's activity.
timeline.rtl: The line runs down the right in Arabic, and Latin names keep their own order.
timeline.when_not: For a conversation people reply to; use the comment thread.
timeline.do_1: Name the actor and the action in plain words.
timeline.do_2: Use the compact variant for long logs.
timeline.dont_1: Do not colour every entry; keep tones for what matters.
timeline.dont_2: Do not mix time orders in one feed.

alternative.comment_thread: For a discussion people reply to.

bar_list.headline: What leads, at a glance.
bar_list.intro: People read the ranking first and the numbers second, without a chart's axes.
bar_list.what: Ranked rows with a value and a proportional bar.
bar_list.when: Use it for top lists: cities, products, pages, sources.
bar_list.rtl: The bars grow from the right in Arabic, and the values sit at the left end.
bar_list.when_not: For trends over time; use a line or bar chart.
bar_list.do_1: Keep the list short: five to ten rows.
bar_list.do_2: Format the values in the unit people expect.
bar_list.dont_1: Do not mix units in one list.
bar_list.dont_2: Do not rely on the bar alone; keep the value visible.

button_group.headline: Related actions, held together.
button_group.intro: Buttons that belong together read as one control, so people see the choice at once.
button_group.when: Use it for a small set of related actions or a view switch.
button_group.rtl: The first button sits on the right in Arabic.
button_group.when_not: For one main action with others behind it; use the split button.
button_group.do_1: Keep the group to two to five buttons.
button_group.do_2: Name the group for screen readers.
button_group.dont_1: Do not mix primary and secondary looks in one group.
button_group.dont_2: Do not put unrelated actions side by side.

alternative.split_button: For one action with a menu of others.

meter.headline: A level, read in one look.
meter.intro: People see how full or how good something is, and the colour tells them whether to act.
meter.what: A bar showing one value on a known scale.
meter.when: Use it for storage, quotas, scores and fill levels.
meter.rtl: The bar fills from the right in Arabic.
meter.when_not: For a task that is still running; use a progress bar.
meter.do_1: Set low, high and optimum so the colour means something.
meter.do_2: Write the value beside the label.
meter.dont_1: Do not use colour alone to say it is critical.
meter.dont_2: Do not use it for an unbounded number.

alternative.progress_bar: For a task moving towards done.
alternative.stacked_meter: For the parts that fill a quota.

result.headline: Say how it went, then what is next.
result.intro: After a payment, a submission or an import, people see the outcome and the one thing to do now.
result.what: A centred outcome with an icon, a title, a line and actions.
result.when: Use it at the end of a flow or in place of a panel's content.
result.rtl: Text and actions centre the same way in Arabic; the icon never mirrors.
result.when_not: For a brief confirmation over the page; use a toast.
result.do_1: Write the title as what happened, in past tense.
result.do_2: Offer the next step as the first action.
result.dont_1: Do not show a success without saying what succeeded.
result.dont_2: Do not leave a pending state without a way out when it takes long.

alternative.empty_state: For a place with nothing in it yet.
alternative.error_state: For a failed load with a retry.

loading_overlay.headline: Hold the region, not the page.
loading_overlay.intro: While one card or table saves, people see it is busy and cannot change it, and the rest of the page stays usable.
loading_overlay.what: A translucent layer with a spinner over one region.
loading_overlay.when: Use it while a region saves or refreshes and its content must not change.
loading_overlay.rtl: The message centres the same way in Arabic.
loading_overlay.when_not: For a first load with nothing to show yet; use a skeleton.
loading_overlay.do_1: Say what is happening in the message.
loading_overlay.dont_1: Do not cover the whole page for one region's work.
loading_overlay.dont_2: Do not leave it up after the work fails; show the error.

alternative.page_skeleton: For content still on its way.
alternative.inline_loading: For a small status beside an action.

scroll_area.headline: Long content, in a calm box.
scroll_area.intro: People see there is more by the faded edge and scroll it by touch, wheel or keyboard.
scroll_area.what: A bounded region that scrolls, its edges fading.
scroll_area.when: Use it for terms, logs and rows of chips that would push the page.
scroll_area.rtl: Horizontal content starts on the right in Arabic.
scroll_area.when_not: For a whole page; let the page scroll.
scroll_area.do_1: Name the region so keyboard users know what they scroll.
scroll_area.do_2: Set a height that shows a few full lines.
scroll_area.dont_2: Do not hide actions inside one.

alternative.carousel: For a few cards to browse.
alternative.drawer: For long content in its own panel.

truncate.headline: Show the start; open the rest.
truncate.intro: Long descriptions stay short in lists, and people open the whole text only when they want it.
truncate.what: Text clamped to a few lines, with a way to read all of it.
truncate.when: Use it for reviews, notes and descriptions in cards and tables.
truncate.rtl: Arabic letters stay joined at the cut, and the button sits at the reading start.
truncate.when_not: For text people must read in full, such as terms; show it.
truncate.do_1: Pick a line count that keeps the first sentence whole.
truncate.do_2: Use the tooltip mode for single-line names in tables.
truncate.dont_1: Do not cut numbers or prices.
truncate.dont_2: Do not put links inside clamped text.

alternative.accordion: For sections people open one by one.
alternative.tooltip: For a short hint on a control.

histogram_chart.headline: See the shape of your numbers.
histogram_chart.intro: Hand it the raw values; it counts them into equal bins so the peak, the spread and the long tail show at a glance.
histogram_chart.what: A chart of touching columns, one per range of values, as tall as its count.
histogram_chart.when: Use it for order sizes, response times, ages and any spread of one measure.
histogram_chart.rtl: Bins run from the right in Arabic, smallest first.

box_plot_chart.headline: Compare whole spreads, not just averages.
box_plot_chart.intro: Each box holds the middle half of a group, the line marks its median, and the rings flag the cases that stand apart.
box_plot_chart.what: A chart of boxes and whiskers that summarises each group's values.
box_plot_chart.when: Use it to compare delivery times, prices or scores across cities, teams or products.
box_plot_chart.rtl: Groups run from the right in Arabic; the value axis sits on the right.

range_bar_chart.headline: Every span, from its low to its high.
range_bar_chart.intro: Floating bars start where each range starts and end where it ends, standing or lying along the categories.
range_bar_chart.what: A chart of bars that float between two values per category.
range_bar_chart.when: Use it for daily temperatures, price bands, shift hours and any minimum to maximum.
range_bar_chart.rtl: Categories run from the right in Arabic, and lying bars grow from the right.

bullet_chart.headline: Progress and target, in one line.
bullet_chart.intro: A bar shows where you are, a tick shows where you are heading, and quiet bands show what good looks like.
bullet_chart.what: A row per measure with its value bar, target tick and qualitative bands.
bullet_chart.when: Use it on dashboards where a gauge would take too much room: sales goals, sign-ups, satisfaction.
bullet_chart.rtl: The scale grows from the right in Arabic; the value sits at the left end.

sankey_chart.headline: See where the flow goes.
sankey_chart.intro: Bands as wide as their flow show which paths carry the most, from the first step to the last.
sankey_chart.what: A chart of stages joined by bands sized by how much passes between them.
sankey_chart.when: Use it for traffic sources to outcomes, budgets to spending, and other many-to-many flows.
sankey_chart.rtl: Stages run from the right in Arabic.

sunburst_chart.headline: Every level of the whole, at once.
sunburst_chart.intro: Categories sit at the centre and their products ring them, so the big shares and their sources read together.
sunburst_chart.what: A chart of nested slices: each ring splits the slice inside it.
sunburst_chart.when: Use it for revenue by category and product, spend by team and person, and other two- or three-level breakdowns.
sunburst_chart.rtl: Like a pie, the rings read clockwise from the top in every language.

timeline_chart.headline: The whole plan on one line of time.
timeline_chart.intro: Each task is a bar from its first day to its last, in its team's lane, with today marked so the next step is plain.
timeline_chart.what: A chart of tasks as bars along a date scale, grouped in lanes.
timeline_chart.when: Use it for launch plans, roadmaps, bookings and any work that runs between two dates.
timeline_chart.rtl: Time runs from the right in Arabic.

choropleth_map.headline: Where it happens, at a glance.
choropleth_map.intro: Each region takes a shade of your accent by its value; you bring the map, so it fits your cities, branches or delivery zones.
choropleth_map.what: A map of regions shaded in five steps by a value.
choropleth_map.when: Use it for orders by district, sales by branch area, and coverage by delivery zone.
choropleth_map.rtl: A map is never mirrored; its scale reads from the right in Arabic.

scatter_chart.headline: Spot the pattern between two numbers.
scatter_chart.intro: Every point sits where its two values meet, so clusters, trends and outliers show at a glance.
scatter_chart.what: A chart of points placed by two numbers, optionally sized by a third.
scatter_chart.when: Use it for price against sales, time against rating, or any two measures you want to compare.
scatter_chart.rtl: The horizontal axis runs from the right in Arabic, and the value axis sits on the right.

heatmap_chart.headline: Busy and quiet, at a glance.
heatmap_chart.intro: Each cell takes a deeper shade as its value grows, so peaks stand out across the whole grid.
heatmap_chart.what: A grid of cells shaded by value, one per row and column category.
heatmap_chart.when: Use it for orders by hour and weekday, tickets by team and status, or any two-way breakdown.
heatmap_chart.rtl: Columns run from the right in Arabic, with row names on the right.

calendar_heatmap.headline: Every day of the year, in one view.
calendar_heatmap.intro: Streaks, busy weeks and quiet spells show at once, and each day names its value when you point at it.
calendar_heatmap.what: A calendar of days shaded by their value, with a column per week.
calendar_heatmap.when: Use it for orders per day, logins, deliveries or any daily habit.
calendar_heatmap.rtl: Weeks run from the right in Arabic, and the week starts on the locale's first day.

gauge_chart.headline: How close are we to the goal?
gauge_chart.intro: The ring fills toward the target mark, and the figure in the middle says exactly where you stand.
gauge_chart.what: A three-quarter ring that fills with a value, with a mark at the target.
gauge_chart.when: Use it for sales against a target, a budget used, or a score out of a maximum.
gauge_chart.rtl: A gauge reads the same in both directions; its figures follow the locale's digits.

waterfall_chart.headline: From one figure to the next, step by step.
waterfall_chart.intro: Each bar floats from the running total by its change, so you see exactly what raised the result and what held it back.
waterfall_chart.what: A chart that bridges a start total to an end total through its changes.
waterfall_chart.when: Use it for profit from one quarter to the next, budget against actual, or stock in and out.
waterfall_chart.rtl: Steps run from the right in Arabic; every change is written with its sign, not shown by colour alone.

candlestick_chart.headline: Every swing of the price, period by period.
candlestick_chart.intro: Each candle shows where the price opened, closed and travelled in between, with the volume traded beneath.
candlestick_chart.what: A chart of candles, one per period, from the open, high, low and close prices.
candlestick_chart.when: Use it for share prices, exchange rates, or any price that moves within a period.
candlestick_chart.rtl: Periods run from the right in Arabic; a rise is hollow and a fall is filled, so direction never rests on colour.

highlight.headline: Show why it matched.
highlight.intro: Search terms light up in the results, matched the way people type: without vowel marks, in any case.
highlight.what: A text with its search terms marked.
highlight.when: Use it in search results, filtered lists and command palettes.
highlight.rtl: Arabic letters stay joined across a mark's edges, and vowel marks stay on their letters.
highlight.when_not: For emphasis the author chose; use bold text.
highlight.do_1: Pass the same text people searched for.
highlight.do_2: Match several terms at once when the search splits them.
highlight.dont_1: Do not change the text to fit the match.
highlight.dont_2: Do not add padding or weight to the mark.

alternative.tag_input: For typing several terms as tags.

number_value.headline: Every number, in the customer's own digits.
number_value.intro: Amounts, counts, shares and sizes read the way the customer reads them: their locale, their digits, their currency.
number_value.what: Small components that write a number, a percent, a size or an amount.
number_value.when: Use them wherever a figure is shown: tables, cards, summaries.
number_value.rtl: Numbers keep their order inside Arabic text, in Latin or Arabic-Indic digits as set.
number_value.when_not: For a figure people edit; use the number or money field.
number_value.do_1: Pass raw numbers and let the component format them.
number_value.do_2: Use compact notation for large figures in tight spaces.
number_value.dont_1: Do not format numbers by hand with string templates.
number_value.dont_2: Do not mix digit systems on one screen.

stepper.headline: Every step, in its place.
stepper.intro: People see where they are in a checkout, an import or a setup, what is done and what is left, and can go back to a finished step.
stepper.what: The ordered steps of one task, with the current one marked.
stepper.when: Use it for checkouts, imports, onboarding and any form split into steps.
stepper.rtl: The steps run from the right and the connectors fill towards the left; numbers follow the digits setting.
stepper.when_not: For moving between pages; use tabs or a sidebar.
stepper.do_1: Keep step names to one or two words.
stepper.do_2: Let people go back to a finished step.
stepper.dont_1: Do not use more than seven steps.
stepper.dont_2: Do not let people skip ahead past a step that is not done.

alternative.tabs: For sections people visit in any order.

countdown.headline: Time, counted calmly.
countdown.intro: People see how long is left or how long has passed, in their digits, and hear it once a minute, not every second.
countdown.what: A countdown to a moment, or a stopwatch from one.
countdown.when: Use it for offers, booking holds, auctions and call or task timers.
countdown.rtl: The digits keep their hh:mm:ss order inside Arabic text.
countdown.when_not: For a time of day; write the time.
countdown.do_1: Say what ends in the label.
countdown.do_2: Act on `onComplete`, not on the digits.
countdown.dont_1: Do not use a countdown to pressure people.

alternative.date_label: For when something happened or is due.

qr_code.headline: Point a camera, and it opens.
qr_code.intro: People pay an invoice, join a network or open a page by scanning, with the same words on screen for anyone who cannot.
qr_code.what: A text or link drawn as a QR code.
qr_code.when: Use it for payment links, check-in, Wi-Fi and app downloads.
qr_code.rtl: A QR code never mirrors; the caption reads from the right in Arabic.
qr_code.when_not: For a link people click on the same device; use a link.
qr_code.do_1: Say what the code opens next to it.
qr_code.do_2: Use level H when it may be printed small or partly covered.
qr_code.dont_1: Do not invert the colours in dark mode.
qr_code.dont_2: Do not encode secrets people should not share.

alternative.link: For opening it on this device.

listbox.headline: Every option in view.
listbox.intro: People see all the choices at once and pick one or several, without opening a menu.
listbox.what: An always-visible list of options with checkmarks.
listbox.when: Use it in side panels, settings and pickers with a handful of options.
listbox.rtl: Checkmarks sit at the reading end and the list reads from the right in Arabic.
listbox.when_not: For a long list in a tight form; use a select or a combo box.
listbox.do_1: Group long lists into titled sections.
listbox.do_2: Add a description when labels alone are unclear.
listbox.dont_1: Do not use it for actions; use a menu.
listbox.dont_2: Do not mix single and multiple choice in one list.

alternative.select: For a closed list behind a button.
alternative.checkbox_group: For a few yes-or-no options in a form.

tab_bar.headline: The app's main places, under a thumb.
tab_bar.intro: On a phone, people move between the main sections with one tap at the bottom of the screen, and see what needs them by the badges.
tab_bar.what: A bottom bar of up to five main destinations.
tab_bar.when: Use it as the main navigation of a phone app or mobile web layout.
tab_bar.rtl: Tabs start from the right in Arabic.
tab_bar.when_not: For more than five places or on wide screens; use the sidebar.
tab_bar.do_1: Name each tab in one or two words.
tab_bar.do_2: Use badges for counts that need action.
tab_bar.dont_1: Do not put actions in the tab bar.
tab_bar.dont_2: Do not hide the bar on scroll without a way back.

alternative.sidebar: For many places on wide screens.

collection_engine.headline: One engine behind every data view.
collection_engine.intro: useCollection holds the columns, sort, filter, group, selection, paging, density and saved views, computes them on the client or hands a server a plain query, and remembers them by a key.
collection_engine.tags: Headless · Client or server · Persistence · Saved views
collection_engine.what: A headless React hook shared by web and native.
collection_engine.when: Use it to drive DataView, DataTable, DataGrid or a view of your own from one state.
collection_engine.rtl: The engine has no direction; text sorts by the locale's own collation.

data_view.headline: Every way to see your records, from one toolbar.
data_view.intro: Search, filter with and/or rules, sort by several columns, group, arrange the columns and save the result as a view; then switch between table, grid, list, cards and a kanban board without losing any of it. Every view scrolls ten thousand rows (only what is on screen is drawn), server mode sends the query to a server adapter and loads more as you scroll, and under 600 px of its own width the table turns into cards. Rows reorder, expand, edit in place and open in a side panel from any view.
data_view.tags: Saved views · Rule builder · Multi-sort · Group · Board · Row tools · Server mode · 10k rows · Export
data_view.what: A toolbar and the table, grid, list, cards and board views of one collection.
data_view.when: Use it for any index people search, slice and come back to: orders, customers, products.
data_view.rtl: The toolbar, the pinned columns and the drag all mirror in Arabic; amounts keep their digits' direction.

period_picker.headline: This period, and the one before.
period_picker.intro: Ready ranges for the usual questions, the calendar for the rest, and one switch to set the numbers beside last period or last year.
period_picker.what: A row of controls for a dashboard period: a preset, a custom range and the comparison.
period_picker.when: Use it above a dashboard or in a widget’s controls row, wherever charts and KPIs read one period.
period_picker.rtl: The controls run from the right in Arabic, the switch thumb moves to the left when on, and dates read in Arabic order.

tracker_strip.headline: Every day of uptime, in one line.
tracker_strip.intro: A row of quiet cells shows how a service did, period by period; the bad days stand out without a chart.
tracker_strip.what: An even row of cells, one per period, filled by its state, with the uptime worked out from them.
tracker_strip.when: Use it on status pages and service dashboards, and anywhere a run of days matters more than one figure.
tracker_strip.rtl: The oldest period sits at the right in Arabic and the arrow keys follow the reading direction.

dashboard_grid.headline: A dashboard each reader arranges.
dashboard_grid.intro: Widgets sit in a responsive 12-column grid. In edit mode readers drag, move and resize them, and the layout is saved for next time.
dashboard_grid.tags: Drag and drop · Resize · Saved layouts
dashboard_grid.what: A grid of dashboard tiles with an edit mode: a slim toolbar on each tile to drag, move and step its size, and an edge to drag between the four sizes, saved through a layout port.
dashboard_grid.when: Use it for home and analytics dashboards where each person watches different numbers.
dashboard_grid.rtl: Tiles flow from the right in Arabic; earlier and later follow the reading order, and the resize edge is on the left.

form_error_summary.headline: Every problem, one step from its fix.
form_error_summary.intro: After a failed send, a summary lists what is wrong. Each item jumps to its field, and focus lands on the summary first.
form_error_summary.what: A danger box above a form listing each error as a link to its field.
form_error_summary.when: Use it on long forms and checkout steps, where an error can sit out of view.
form_error_summary.rtl: The list reads from the right in Arabic, each field's name before its message.

checkbox_field.headline: Consent, in a sentence.
checkbox_field.intro: Its label is its children, so a consent can read as a full sentence with emphasis.
checkbox_field.what: A Checkbox with its label as children, for a schema form's field binding.
checkbox_field.when: Use it for a consent or terms box inside a form written against the binding.
checkbox_field.rtl: The box sits at the start of the line, which is the right in Arabic.

text_area_field.headline: A longer answer, bound to the form.
text_area_field.intro: It takes the binding's value, handlers and error as they come, and draws the Text area.
text_area_field.what: A Text area for a schema form's field binding.
text_area_field.when: Use it for a note, a reason or a message inside a form written against the binding.
text_area_field.rtl: The text starts at the right in Arabic, and the count follows the reading direction.

dropdown.headline: A short menu, written where it is used.
dropdown.intro: Each item can carry a second line and a danger look, and a menu can hold one choice.
dropdown.what: A button that opens a menu of actions or choices.
dropdown.when: Use it for an account menu or a locale switcher written inline; for a menu built from data, use Menu.
dropdown.rtl: The menu opens under the button and its items read from the right in Arabic.

heading.headline: The outline and the look, kept apart.
heading.intro: The level is required, so every heading is placed on purpose; the type changes only how it looks.
heading.what: A heading from level 1 to 6, drawn in the type scale.
heading.when: Use it for every title of a page or a section; pick the level from the outline, then the type from the design.
heading.rtl: A heading aligns to the start, which is the right in Arabic.

kiosk_surface.headline: A screen that looks after itself.
kiosk_surface.intro: It resets when nobody touches it, keeps controls within reach and can speak what changes.
kiosk_surface.what: A wrapper that puts a screen in kiosk mode.
kiosk_surface.when: Use it for a self-service kiosk, a lane screen or a gate screen that nobody attends.
kiosk_surface.rtl: The layout follows the reading direction; announcements speak in the provider's locale.

turnstile.headline: Keep bots out without a puzzle.
turnstile.intro: The widget loads Cloudflare's script once, puts its token in a hidden field and the server checks it.
turnstile.what: Cloudflare's bot check, drawn where the form needs it.
turnstile.when: Use it on a public form that bots abuse: sign up, contact or password reset.
turnstile.rtl: Cloudflare draws the widget in the browser's language; it sits at the start of the form row.

chart_legend.headline: Which colour is which.
chart_legend.intro: A hidden series reads as a hollow swatch and a struck label, so the state never rests on colour alone.
chart_legend.what: The legend every chart draws, for one set apart from its chart.
chart_legend.when: Use it when a legend sits away from its chart, or for a chart composed from Recharts directly.
chart_legend.rtl: The row wraps from the right in Arabic, and the swatch stays before its label.

chart_tooltip.headline: The numbers behind the point.
chart_tooltip.intro: Values are written in the locale with tabular figures, beside a dot or a short bar in the series' colour.
chart_tooltip.what: The tooltip card every chart passes to Recharts.
chart_tooltip.when: Use it as the tooltip content of a chart composed from Recharts directly.
chart_tooltip.rtl: Each line reads from the right in Arabic, with the value at the line's end.

polar_chart.headline: See which part of the cycle runs hot.
polar_chart.intro: Every weekday or month gets the same slice; how far it reaches is how much happened, so the peaks stand out at a glance.
polar_chart.what: A chart of equal slices whose length is their value.
polar_chart.when: For a value over a cycle: weekdays, hours or months.
polar_chart.rtl: Slices keep their clockwise order; the names sit outside the ring and read in Arabic.
polar_chart.when_not: To compare parts of a whole; use a pie chart.
polar_chart.do_1: Use it for a cycle of five to twelve steps.
polar_chart.do_2: Keep to two series so the slices stay wide.
polar_chart.dont_1: Don't use it for categories with no order.
polar_chart.dont_2: Don't make people read exact numbers off it; the tooltip and table give them.

alternative.radar_chart: To compare profiles across several measures.
alternative.bar_chart: To compare exact values side by side.

waffle_chart.headline: A hundred squares make the whole.
waffle_chart.intro: Each part fills its run of squares, so shares are counted rather than guessed, and the legend gives each part's value and percentage.
waffle_chart.what: A grid of squares that shows how a whole splits into parts.
waffle_chart.when: For two to five parts of one whole, such as payment methods or stock states.
waffle_chart.rtl: Squares fill from the right in Arabic, in reading order, and the legend reads right to left.
waffle_chart.when_not: To show change over time; use a bar or line chart.
waffle_chart.do_1: Keep to five parts or fewer.
waffle_chart.do_2: Order the parts from largest to smallest.
waffle_chart.dont_1: Don't show parts that do not add up to one whole.
waffle_chart.dont_2: Don't rely on colour alone; keep the legend on.

alternative.pie_chart: For the same shares as slices.
alternative.stacked_meter: For the shares as one compact bar.

marquee.headline: Keep the strip moving, never in the way.
marquee.intro: Logos and short news glide past and stop under the pointer, on focus or with the pause button; with reduced motion they simply sit still.
marquee.what: A strip whose content scrolls on a seamless loop.
marquee.when: For partner logos, delivery notices and short offers that are fine to miss.
marquee.rtl: In Arabic the strip moves to the right, toward where reading starts.
marquee.when_not: For anything people must read to act; put it in a banner.
marquee.do_1: Keep each item short enough to read while it moves.
marquee.do_2: Name the strip so screen readers know what it holds.
marquee.dont_1: Don't put the only link to something in a moving strip.
marquee.dont_2: Don't speed it up to fit more in.

alternative.carousel: For a few large items people step through.
alternative.system_banner: For one message everyone must see.

barcode.headline: Print it, scan it, ship it.
barcode.intro: Product numbers and parcel labels are encoded by our own Code 128 and EAN-13 encoders, with the check digit worked out for you.
barcode.what: A value drawn as a linear barcode with its digits.
barcode.when: For product labels, packing slips, shelf tags and receipts.
barcode.rtl: A barcode never mirrors: bars and digits read left to right in Arabic too.
barcode.when_not: For links or long text; use a QR code.
barcode.do_1: Show the digits under the bars for anyone typing them in.
barcode.do_2: Leave the light margin around the bars when printing.
barcode.dont_1: Don't invert the colours in dark mode.
barcode.dont_2: Don't stretch the bars to fit a box.

alternative.copy_button: To copy the number instead of scanning it.

aspect_ratio.headline: The space is ready before the picture arrives.
aspect_ratio.intro: Give a photo or video its shape up front and the page holds still while it loads, on any width.
aspect_ratio.what: A full-width box held at a width to height ratio.
aspect_ratio.when: For product photos, videos, maps and cover images.
aspect_ratio.rtl: Nothing changes in Arabic; the box keeps its shape.
aspect_ratio.when_not: For text, which should set its own height.
aspect_ratio.do_1: Use one ratio for every photo in a grid.
aspect_ratio.do_2: Crop the picture to the box, not the box to the picture.
aspect_ratio.dont_1: Don't put long text in a fixed box.
aspect_ratio.dont_2: Don't use a ratio that cuts off the product.

alternative.thumbnail: For a small picture with a fallback.
alternative.layout: For arranging blocks without a ratio.

page_indicator.headline: Know where you are at a glance.
page_indicator.intro: The current page stretches into a bar; press a dot to jump to its page, or leave the dots to show the place.
page_indicator.tags: Dots · Press to jump · Reduced motion
page_indicator.what: A row of dots, one per page, the current one longer.
page_indicator.when: Under carousels, onboarding screens and image viewers with a few pages.
page_indicator.rtl: Page one is on the right in Arabic, and the dots fill toward the left.
page_indicator.when_not: For more than about eight pages; use pagination.
page_indicator.do_1: Keep the dots close to what they page.
page_indicator.do_2: Name each dot so it is clear where it goes.
page_indicator.dont_1: Don't use the dots as the only way forward.
page_indicator.dont_2: Don't colour dots to mean anything but the current page.

alternative.stepper: For steps people must finish in order.

back_to_top.headline: One tap from the bottom to the top.
back_to_top.intro: It waits until people have scrolled a fair way, then takes them back and puts keyboard focus where the page begins.
back_to_top.what: A floating button that scrolls back to the top.
back_to_top.when: On long product lists, articles and order histories.
back_to_top.rtl: It sits at the bottom left in Arabic, at the end of the line.
back_to_top.when_not: On short pages that fit in two screens.
back_to_top.do_1: Show it only after a real scroll.
back_to_top.do_2: Keep it clear of chat and cart buttons.
back_to_top.dont_1: Don't cover content people need at the corner.
back_to_top.dont_2: Don't add a second one inside the same page.

footer.headline: Everything people look for at the end of the page.
footer.intro: Help, policies and contact sit in clear columns that stack on a phone, with the copyright and legal links on one quiet row.
footer.what: The site's footer: brand, link columns and a bottom row.
footer.when: At the end of every page of a shop or marketing site.
footer.rtl: The brand starts on the right in Arabic and the columns read right to left.
footer.when_not: In an app screen; use the tab bar.
footer.do_1: Group links under headings people recognise.
footer.do_2: Keep returns and contact links one tap away.
footer.dont_1: Don't repeat the whole main menu.
footer.dont_2: Don't hide legal links in small grey text no one can read.

alternative.navigation_menu: For the main navigation at the top.

questionnaire_card.headline: Ask before you guess.
questionnaire_card.intro: When a request is unclear, the assistant asks a few short questions in one card, one at a time, and shows the answers before anything is sent.
questionnaire_card.tags: One question per step · Other · Summary
questionnaire_card.what: A card that asks single-choice, multiple-choice and free-text questions in steps, then summarises the answers.
questionnaire_card.when: When an assistant needs two to five details before it drafts an offer, a report or a reply.
questionnaire_card.rtl: Back points to the right in Arabic, options and summaries read from the right, and the step count keeps its numbers.
questionnaire_card.when_not: For a long form people fill in on their own; use a form with sections.
questionnaire_card.do_1: Keep it to five questions or fewer, each answerable in seconds.
questionnaire_card.do_2: Offer "Other" when your options may not cover every case.
questionnaire_card.dont_1: Don't ask what the assistant already knows from the conversation.
questionnaire_card.dont_2: Don't make every question required; let people skip.

alternative.stepper: For a long task with named stages.
alternative.radio_group: For one question on its own.

model_picker.headline: The right model, plainly described.
model_picker.intro: Each model shows what it is good at, how much it can read at once, and why it is unavailable when it is.
model_picker.what: A select whose options are AI models, with tags, context size, a New or Beta badge and a reason when disabled.
model_picker.when: In an assistant's composer or settings, where people choose which model answers.
model_picker.rtl: The list and badges read from the right; model names and sizes keep their own direction.
model_picker.when_not: When the product picks the model for people; don't ask.
model_picker.do_1: Describe each model by what it is good at, in a few words.
model_picker.do_2: Say why a model is unavailable, such as the plan it needs.
model_picker.dont_1: Don't list more than about ten models.
model_picker.dont_2: Don't hide unavailable models people may want to upgrade for.

alternative.select: For a plain list of choices.
alternative.chip: To show the model in use without changing it.

voice_input.headline: Speak instead of typing.
voice_input.intro: Press the microphone, speak, press again. The bars show it hears you, and every step, from asking for the microphone to processing, is announced.
voice_input.tags: Microphone · Live level · Port and drivers
voice_input.what: A toggle button that records through a recorder port: the browser's microphone on web, a mock driver on native until a native one is chosen.
voice_input.when: In a composer or a notes field where dictating is faster than typing.
voice_input.rtl: The button sits at the start in Arabic and the status follows it; the level bars are symmetric.
voice_input.when_not: For long recordings or calls; use a dedicated recorder.
voice_input.do_1: Show what happens to the recording, such as the transcript, once it is processed.
voice_input.do_2: Tell people how to allow the microphone when it is blocked.
voice_input.dont_1: Don't start recording without a press.
voice_input.dont_2: Don't keep a recording after it is cancelled.

alternative.icon_button: For a one-off action with no recording.

conversation_list.headline: Pick up any conversation where you left it.
conversation_list.intro: Past chats with the assistant sit under Today, Yesterday and the week before, pinned ones on top, each with its last words and how long ago it was.
conversation_list.what: A list of past AI conversations, grouped by when they last changed.
conversation_list.when: In the side panel of an assistant, a support inbox or a shopping helper.
conversation_list.rtl: Rows, times and the menu button mirror in Arabic; arrow keys follow the reading direction.
conversation_list.when_not: For a list of records that are not conversations; use the list box.
conversation_list.do_1: Title each conversation from its first question.
conversation_list.dont_1: Don't show the whole last message; a line is enough.
conversation_list.dont_2: Don't hide pinned conversations inside the day groups.

alternative.listbox: To choose items that are not conversations.

message_actions.headline: Every answer, one tap from useful.
message_actions.intro: Under each answer people copy it, ask again, edit their question or say whether it helped; the thumbs say when they are pressed.
message_actions.what: A row of icon buttons under an assistant's message.
message_actions.when: Under every answer an assistant writes.
message_actions.rtl: The row starts at the right in Arabic and the arrow keys follow it.
message_actions.when_not: For emoji reactions on people's messages; use the reaction button.
message_actions.do_1: Keep the same actions in the same order under every answer.
message_actions.do_2: Use the rating to improve answers, and say so.
message_actions.dont_1: Don't ask for a reason on every thumbs down.
message_actions.dont_2: Don't show retry on an answer that is still being written.

alternative.reaction_button: For emoji reactions with a count.

message_scroller.headline: Read back without losing the thread.
message_scroller.intro: While people are at the bottom the answer streams into view; when they scroll up to read, it stays put and a button says how many new messages wait below.
message_scroller.tags: Sticks to bottom · Jump button · Live region
message_scroller.what: The scrolling area of a conversation.
message_scroller.when: Around the messages of an assistant or a support chat.
message_scroller.rtl: The jump button stays centred and its words read right to left in Arabic.
message_scroller.when_not: For a page or a panel that is not a conversation; use the scroll area.
message_scroller.do_1: Give it a height so it can scroll.
message_scroller.do_2: Give each message its own child, so the new-message count is right.
message_scroller.dont_1: Don't pull people down while they read further up.
message_scroller.dont_2: Don't animate the jump for people who asked for less motion.

prompt_suggestions.headline: Show people what to ask.
prompt_suggestions.intro: A few good first questions as cards or chips; one tap sends it, so nobody stares at an empty box.
prompt_suggestions.when: On an empty conversation, or after an answer to suggest the next step.
prompt_suggestions.rtl: Cards start at the right in Arabic and the scrolling row starts there too.
prompt_suggestions.when_not: To filter a list; use chips or a segmented control.
prompt_suggestions.do_1: Write each suggestion as the person would ask it.
prompt_suggestions.do_2: Offer three to six; fewer are easier to read.
prompt_suggestions.dont_1: Don't suggest what the assistant cannot do.
prompt_suggestions.dont_2: Don't keep old suggestions once the conversation moved on.

alternative.chip: For a tag or a filter.

shimmer.headline: Show the assistant is working, quietly.
shimmer.intro: A soft light sweeps across "Thinking…" in the reading direction, or over placeholder lines while a longer answer loads; it stands still for people who asked for less motion.
shimmer.what: A loading shimmer over text, or over placeholder lines.
shimmer.when: While an assistant thinks, searches or writes.
shimmer.rtl: The light sweeps from right to left in Arabic, and the text is never drawn letter by letter.
shimmer.when_not: For a page that loads; use the skeleton.
shimmer.do_1: Say what is happening: Searching orders, Reading the invoice.
shimmer.do_2: Replace it with the answer as soon as the first words arrive.
shimmer.dont_1: Don't shimmer more than one line of text at a time.
shimmer.dont_2: Don't leave it running when the request failed.

alternative.skeleton: For the shape of content that is loading.

media_player.headline: Play it here, in your own controls.
media_player.intro: The browser or the phone plays the file; the controls are the house ones, in the customer's language and digits, with captions and speeds, and on the web the shortcuts people already know.
media_player.what: Controls over a video or audio file: play, a timeline with what is loaded, the time, volume, speed, captions and full screen.
media_player.when: For product videos, tutorials, voice notes and recorded calls inside the app.
media_player.rtl: The controls and timeline stay left to right in Arabic, as on YouTube and every system player: time runs left to right on a media timeline, and the play icon is not mirrored. Names and the speed menu are Arabic.
media_player.when_not: For a moving background or a decorative loop; use a plain video without controls.
media_player.do_1: Add captions to every video with speech.
media_player.do_2: Name the player after what it plays.
media_player.dont_1: Don't start playing with sound on its own.
media_player.dont_2: Don't put two players side by side that play at once.

alternative.attachment_card: To offer the file to download instead of playing it.

time_clock.headline: A time, set the way a clock reads.
time_clock.intro: Press the hour, then the minute, on a face people have read all their lives. Keys step it, and screen readers hear the whole time.
time_clock.what: An analogue face for picking a time of day: the hours ring, then the minutes.
time_clock.when: For pickup, delivery and booking times on a touch screen, beside or inside a time field.
time_clock.rtl: The face is not mirrored in Arabic: clocks run clockwise everywhere. The numerals use the customer's digits, and the time above reads hours then minutes.
time_clock.when_not: For a time typed from memory, such as a date of birth's hour; use a time field.
time_clock.do_1: Use minute steps that match your slots, such as 15.
time_clock.do_2: Pair it with a time field so the time can also be typed.
time_clock.dont_1: Don't use it for durations; it picks a time of day.
time_clock.dont_2: Don't hide which half of the day is chosen.

alternative.wheel_picker: For a compact wheel on phones.

angle_slider.headline: Turn it to the angle you want.
angle_slider.intro: Drag the hand round the dial or step it with the keys. The angle is shown and spoken in degrees.
angle_slider.what: A circular slider for an angle from 0 to 359 degrees.
angle_slider.when: For a gradient's direction, an image's rotation or a heading.
angle_slider.rtl: The dial is not mirrored in Arabic: an angle is absolute, so 90 degrees points right in every language and the keys turn it clockwise.
angle_slider.when_not: For an amount on a scale; use a slider.
angle_slider.do_1: Show what the angle changes beside the dial.
angle_slider.do_2: Use a step of 15 or 45 when only common angles make sense.
angle_slider.dont_1: Don't use it for values that don't go round.
angle_slider.dont_2: Don't make the dial smaller than a fingertip can drag.

alternative.slider: For a value on a straight scale.

popconfirm.headline: Ask right where it happens.
popconfirm.intro: A short question opens beside the button that raised it, so people confirm a delete or a refund without losing their place, and a slow confirm shows it is working.
popconfirm.what: A popover that asks one yes-or-no question about the control it is anchored to.
popconfirm.when: Before a small, reversible-looking action that deserves a second look: deleting a draft, removing a row, refunding an order.
popconfirm.rtl: The popover follows its trigger to the other side in Arabic, and the buttons keep their reading order with confirm at the end.
popconfirm.when_not: For a decision that needs explaining, a typed name or a list of what will change; use an alert dialog.
popconfirm.do_1: Word the title as the question and the confirm button as the action: "Delete draft?", "Delete".
popconfirm.do_2: Use the danger tone for anything that removes data, so focus starts on cancel.
popconfirm.dont_1: Don't ask for an action people take many times a minute; offer undo instead.
popconfirm.dont_2: Don't put a form or more than one line of detail in it.

alternative.alert_dialog: For a heavier decision that needs the whole screen's attention.
alternative.popover: For rich content anchored to a control that is not a yes-or-no question.

menubar.headline: The desktop menu, in the browser.
menubar.intro: Editors and back-office tools get File, Edit and View menus that people already know: one tab stop, the arrow keys between menus, and checkable view options with their shortcuts.
menubar.what: A horizontal bar of menus, each a list of actions in sections.
menubar.when: In a dense editor or tool with many commands people reach by keyboard: an order editor, a report builder, a page designer.
menubar.rtl: The bar starts from the right in Arabic, the Left and Right keys follow the reading direction, and the menus open from their item's right edge.
menubar.when_not: On a phone, or for a handful of page actions; use a menu or the page's own buttons.
menubar.do_1: Group actions in sections and show their shortcuts.
menubar.do_2: Use checkable actions for view options that stay on.
menubar.dont_1: Don't put navigation between pages in a menubar.
menubar.dont_2: Don't hide an action that is only in the menubar; keep key actions on the page too.

alternative.menu: For one menu of actions behind a button.
alternative.app_header: For the app's top bar with navigation and the account.

floating_panel.headline: A window that stays out of the way.
floating_panel.intro: A chat, a tool palette or a preview floats over the page while people keep working underneath; they drag it aside, resize it, fold it to its title and bring it back.
floating_panel.what: A movable, resizable, non-modal panel with a title bar, minimise and close.
floating_panel.when: For a helper people use alongside the page: support chat, bulk-edit tools, a live preview.
floating_panel.rtl: In Arabic it opens at the bottom left and its resize grip sits at the bottom left corner; the arrow keys still move it the way they point.
floating_panel.when_not: For a task that blocks the page until it is done; use a drawer or a modal.
floating_panel.do_1: Give it a short title that names the tool.
floating_panel.do_2: Open it from a clear button and remember where people left it.
floating_panel.dont_1: Don't open more than one floating panel at a time.
floating_panel.dont_2: Don't cover the page's main action where it first opens.

alternative.side_panel: For a helper docked beside the page that resizes the content.
alternative.drawer: For a task in a panel that blocks the page.

cascader.headline: One path through many levels.
cascader.intro: People pick a country, then a region, then a district in columns side by side, and the field shows the whole path, so the choice is clear at a glance.
cascader.what: A field that picks a path through a tree, one level per column.
cascader.when: When every choice needs its parents: delivery areas, product categories, organisation units.
cascader.rtl: Columns open to the left in Arabic and the path reads right to left with its slash between names; the chevrons mirror.
cascader.when_not: When people pick rows at any level or several at once; use a tree select.
cascader.do_1: Load deep levels on demand when the tree is large.
cascader.do_2: Keep names short so the path fits the field.
cascader.dont_1: Don't use it for more than four or five levels.
cascader.dont_2: Don't mix levels of different kinds in one column.

alternative.tree_select: To pick rows at any level, or several at once.
alternative.select: For one flat list of options.

transfer_list.headline: Move what you need, see what is left.
transfer_list.intro: Two lists side by side show what is available and what is chosen; people tick, filter and move items across, and the counts keep up.
transfer_list.what: Two filterable lists with buttons that move ticked items between them.
transfer_list.when: When people choose many items from a long list and need to see both sides: stock locations, export columns, team members.
transfer_list.rtl: The available list sits on the right in Arabic and the move arrows point to the list they move to.
transfer_list.when_not: For a few options; use a checkbox group or a multi select.
transfer_list.do_1: Name both lists for what they mean here, not just Available and Chosen.
transfer_list.do_2: Keep a filter on long lists.
transfer_list.dont_1: Don't use it when the order of chosen items matters; use a sortable list.
transfer_list.dont_2: Don't put more than a few hundred items in one list.

alternative.multi_select: For several choices in a compact field.
alternative.checkbox_group: For a short list of options to tick.

chat_surface.headline: A whole assistant, in one block.
chat_surface.intro: The conversation scrolls with the newest answer, each answer shows its steps, sources and actions, and starters help people begin.
chat_surface.what: The assistant chat of the AI module, built from the chat parts.
chat_surface.when: Wherever people talk to an assistant: a help panel, a shopping assistant or a back-office copilot.
chat_surface.rtl: Turns, bubbles and actions mirror in Arabic, and Arabic answers keep their shaping.

pricing_table.headline: Plans side by side, priced for the period.
pricing_table.intro: People switch the period and compare plans, the featured plan stands out, and each card ends with its own button.
pricing_table.what: The plan comparison block of the pricing module.
pricing_table.when: On a pricing page, or before a subscription checkout.
pricing_table.rtl: Cards run from the right in Arabic and prices format for the locale.

cart.headline: Everything in the bag, at a glance.
cart.intro: Each line shows its image, variant, quantity and amount, the totals come from pricing, and checkout is one press away.
cart.what: The shopping cart block of the payments module.
cart.when: In a cart page or drawer before checkout.
cart.rtl: Lines and the stepper mirror in Arabic; amounts keep their digits and currency.

checkout.headline: From details to paid, on one page.
checkout.intro: The fields come from the market's address format, shipping options and payment methods are data, and the summary stays beside the form.
checkout.what: The checkout block of the payments module.
checkout.when: The last step of a purchase, after the cart.
checkout.rtl: The form and summary swap sides in Arabic and labels sit at the right.

sign_in.headline: A familiar door, configured per tenant.
sign_in.intro: The tenant chooses its providers and whether a password form shows; the block handles the layout, the waiting state and errors.
sign_in.what: The sign-in block of the identity module.
sign_in.when: On a sign-in page or in a sign-in dialog.
sign_in.rtl: The card mirrors in Arabic; email and password fields keep left-to-right input.

feature_section.headline: Say what it does, in a grid.
feature_section.intro: An eyebrow, a title and an intro over a responsive grid of features, each with an icon, a title and a line.
feature_section.what: The feature section block of the experience module.
feature_section.when: On a landing or product page, under the hero.
feature_section.rtl: The grid starts at the right in Arabic and icons keep their meaning.

cta_section.headline: One clear next step.
cta_section.intro: A raised section with a headline and its buttons, or a newsletter form that thanks people once they subscribe.
cta_section.what: The call-to-action block of the experience module.
cta_section.when: At the end of a landing page or between sections.
cta_section.rtl: Text is centred in both directions and the form mirrors in Arabic.

scheduler.headline: See the week at a glance.
scheduler.intro: People see bookings, shifts and meetings where they fall in the day, spot clashes side by side, and jump between day, week, month and a plain list.
scheduler.what: An event calendar with a time grid, a month grid and an agenda list.
scheduler.when: For appointments, bookings, rosters and team calendars.
scheduler.rtl: The week starts on the locale's first day and runs from the right in Arabic; times and dates use the customer's digits.
scheduler.when_not: To pick one date; use a date picker or a calendar.
scheduler.do_1: Pass the time zone the events belong to.
scheduler.do_2: Limit the hours to the working day when nights are empty.
scheduler.dont_1: Do not use colour alone to say what an event is; name it in the title.
scheduler.dont_2: Do not put long notes in the title; open the event for details.

alternative.timeline_chart: For tasks across weeks on one bar each.

chart_export.headline: Take the chart with you.
chart_export.intro: People save the chart for a report or a message, as it looks on screen or as numbers for a spreadsheet.
chart_export.what: A download menu around any chart.
chart_export.when: Use it on reports and dashboards people share.
chart_export.rtl: The button sits at the reading end, on the left in Arabic.

network_graph.headline: See the connections.
network_graph.intro: Linked nodes pull together and the busiest grow larger, so clusters and hubs stand out.
network_graph.what: A chart of nodes joined by lines, placed by a force layout.
network_graph.when: Use it for teams, service dependencies, referrals and other relationships.
network_graph.rtl: The picture is mirrored in Arabic.

tree_diagram.headline: Every level, one branch at a time.
tree_diagram.intro: Each level is a column and each branch keeps its colour, so people follow a path from the top to the detail.
tree_diagram.what: A chart of nodes joined parent to child, level by level.
tree_diagram.when: Use it for org charts, category trees and decision paths.
tree_diagram.rtl: Levels run from the right in Arabic.

word_cloud.headline: The loudest words, at a glance.
word_cloud.intro: The heaviest words sit large in the middle, so the themes in reviews or searches read in one look.
word_cloud.what: Words set flat, each sized by its weight.
word_cloud.when: Use it for review themes, search terms and survey answers.
word_cloud.rtl: Arabic words are shaped by the platform and the cloud mirrors.

chord_diagram.headline: Who moves where, round one ring.
chord_diagram.intro: Each group's arc is as long as all that leaves and reaches it, and ribbons show every flow between two groups.
chord_diagram.what: A ring of groups with ribbons between them sized by flow.
chord_diagram.when: Use it for plan changes, transfers between branches and trade between regions.
chord_diagram.rtl: Like a pie, the ring reads clockwise from the top in every language.

rating.headline: How was it, in one tap.
rating.intro: People score a visit, a product or a reply in stars, and see the average at a glance.
rating.what: A row of stars that picks a whole score, or shows one with a fraction.
rating.when: Use it for reviews, feedback forms and average scores.
rating.rtl: The first star is on the right in Arabic, and a half star fills from the right.
rating.when_not: For a choice between named options; use a radio group.
rating.do_1: Show the average as a read-only rating with its number.
rating.do_2: Name the rating, such as "Your visit".
rating.dont_1: Do not ask for half stars; people pick whole ones.
rating.dont_2: Do not use colour alone to show the score.

alternative.reaction_button: For a quick reaction to a message.

image.headline: Pictures that never break the page.
image.intro: The space is kept while the picture loads, a blurred copy shows first, and a broken link shows an icon instead.
image.what: A picture as wide as its container, with an optional caption.
image.when: Use it for photos in articles, product pages and cards.
image.rtl: Pictures never mirror; the caption follows the reading direction.

code.headline: Code that reads as code.
code.intro: Commands, keys and file names stand out from the sentence around them.
code.what: A short piece of code inside running text.
code.when: Use it for commands, values and names a person types.
code.rtl: The code stays left to right inside an Arabic sentence.

chat_message.headline: Questions in a bubble, answers on the page.
chat_message.intro: People find their own words at a glance, and long answers read like a document, with files above and actions under them.
chat_message.what: One turn of a conversation with an assistant.
chat_message.when: Use it for every message in an AI chat.
chat_message.rtl: The person's bubble sits on the left in Arabic.
chat_message.when_not: For comments between people on a record; use the comment thread.
chat_message.do_1: Put the turns in a message scroller so new text is followed.
chat_message.do_2: Give the assistant's turn its actions row.
chat_message.dont_1: Do not box the assistant's answer in a bubble.
chat_message.dont_2: Do not show a spinner and the shimmer together.

alternative.comment_thread: For people talking about a record.
alternative.message_scroller: For the scrolling list around the turns.

prompt_input.headline: Ask, attach, send. Stop when you need to.
prompt_input.intro: People write a question, add files and tools, and the same button sends, waits and stops the answer.
prompt_input.what: The box where people write to an assistant.
prompt_input.when: Use it at the foot of every chat or agent screen.
prompt_input.rtl: The toolbar starts at the right in Arabic and the text is right-aligned.
prompt_input.when_not: For a long form field; use the text area.
prompt_input.do_1: Say what the assistant can and cannot do in the footer.
prompt_input.do_2: Show Stop while the answer streams.
prompt_input.dont_1: Do not clear the text when sending fails.
prompt_input.dont_2: Do not crowd the toolbar with more than four actions.

alternative.text_area: For a plain multi-line field in a form.
alternative.mention_input: For text that names people with @.

reasoning.headline: Show the work, without the noise.
reasoning.intro: People see that the assistant is thinking, and can open the steps when they want to check how it got there.
reasoning.what: A folded list of the steps an assistant took.
reasoning.when: Use it above an answer that came from reasoning or tool calls.
reasoning.rtl: The step line runs down the right side in Arabic.
reasoning.when_not: For an activity history with dates; use the timeline.
reasoning.do_1: Write the summary as what was done, such as "Searched 3 files".
reasoning.do_2: Keep it closed by default once the answer is ready.
reasoning.dont_1: Do not put the answer itself in the steps.
reasoning.dont_2: Do not open the trace on every new step.

alternative.disclosure: For any section that shows and hides.

sources.headline: Every claim, one tap from its source.
sources.intro: People see where an answer came from and open the page or document to check it.
sources.what: Citation chips for a web page or a document.
sources.when: Use it under or inside answers that cite sources.
sources.rtl: The chips wrap from the right in Arabic.
sources.when_not: For a plain link in text; use the link.
sources.do_1: Give each source a clear title.
sources.do_2: Add a description so people can preview a page.
sources.dont_1: Do not link to anything but a web page.
sources.dont_2: Do not list sources the answer did not use.

alternative.link: For a link in running text.
alternative.hover_card: For a richer preview of one item.
